🎖️ Today’s Badge: Little Master of Tactile Adaptation

Scratchy Labels and Sticky Clay: Explaining Sensory Needs

🎯 Summary of core objectives:Children with autism often experience emotional distress due to itchy collar tags, sticky or cold textures in art clay, or other tactile discomfort. Encourage children to verbally describe their tactile discomfort and to proactively remove the tags or wear gloves to complete tasks.

📖 Classroom situation adventure story island and questions Arouse empathy · Aware of challenges
🌵 A little hedgehog on the neck and colorful little gloves!

Today, Jia wore her new bright yellow tracksuit to school. But as soon as she entered the classroom, she kept scratching the back of her neck, her face turning bright red. Frustrated, she slammed her textbook on the desk: "It itches! It pricks! I don't want to wear this anymore!" The teacher came over and gently checked, finding a stiff nylon care label sewn onto the back of the collar. The teacher carefully cut off the label with small scissors and placed a soft cotton handkerchief under the collar. Later, during clay art class, the teacher even prepared a pair of thin, transparent baking gloves for Jia, who dislikes sticky textures. Jia touched her neck and smiled happily: "The prickly little hedgehog is gone! I feel so comfortable now!"

🤔 Class discussion guidance questions:If a clothing tag or clay makes you feel very uncomfortable, will constantly getting angry or tearing the clothes help? How can you talk to the teacher to solve the problem?
🎭 Four character situation mini theater 🦁Yu 🐻Jun 🐼He 🦊Jia full-staff drill
🎬 Today's drill scenario:In art class, the clay sticks to their hands, and the tags on their new clothes are itchy. The four little heroes practice expressing their feelings and seeking help!
🦁 Yu Calm and self-disciplined Yu
🎬 Action:When you touch the sticky slime and feel your palms go numb, immediately place both hands flat on the table and take a deep breath, without throwing the slime on the ground.
"Teacher, I feel weird when the clay sticks to the palm of my hand. Can I put on gloves first and then squeeze it?"”
💡 Tips:Guide Yu to actively express tactile defensive feelings and use tools to gradually desensitize them.
🐻 Jun A courageous and responsible young man
🎬 Action:Your neck is itchy from the new clothes. Resist the urge to tear the collar and raise your hand to walk towards the teacher.
"Phew~ I'm about to get angry!"Because the label on the back of my clothes is very prickly, please help me cut it off!”
💡 Tips:Guidance to tell the specific physical reasons before the angry volcano erupts.
🐼 He Gentle and considerate little He
🎬 Action:Put on thin, transparent gloves, happily pick up the yellow clay and knead it into a small ball, with a bright smile.
"When you put on gloves, the clay won't stick to your hands!" I can build a clay castle too! ”
💡 Tips:Help He experience the sense of successful participation brought by tool assistance.
🦊 Jia Enthusiastic and rule-abiding Jia
🎬 Action:Take the cut-off tag and put it in the trash can, straighten your collar, sit up straight and return to your seat.
"The label is cut clean!"When I feel better, I can concentrate on doing art work with everyone!”
💡 Tips:Guide Jia to experience the state of focused learning after eliminating sensory interference.

🏫 Post-it notes on integration tips for regular class instructors:
Parents are reminded to cut off all the back collars and side labels of their children's new school uniforms before the start of school, or to purchase seamless and skin-friendly clothing.
🏠 Home Practice Check-In:
Check the clothes at home that are uncomfortable to wear, and use small scissors with mom and dad to carefully trim the prickly tags!

🔹 Students with autism spectrum disorder (ASD)
Provide three visual solutions: "cut off the label/wear inner sanitary clothing/wear gloves".
🔹 Students with Learning Disabilities (LD)
Use the children's rhyme formula "Prick, scratch, scratch, don't get angry, ask the teacher to cut small labels" to recite to deepen memory.
🔹 Students with Emotional Disorders (EBD)
Guide to take three deep breaths before tearing clothes, and say "My neck is thorny" instead of throwing things.

🔋 Three-minute recharge technique
🏷️ Inspiration Library Special Topic 1: Sensory Regulation and Sensory Adaptation 📌 Field:⚡ Sensory Modulation
🎖️ Today’s Badge: Sensory Charging Butler

🍲 Noisy Places: Asking for a Quiet Recharge Break

🎯 Summary of core objectives:Faced with the crowds at the after-school cooperative, the smell of steamed buns, and the noisy hawking, schoolchildren are prone to multi-sensory overload. Teaching children to recognize brain shutdown warning signs involves giving a "pause" gesture to their peers and retreating to a quiet, well-ventilated area to recharge.

📖 Classroom situation adventure story island and questions Arouse empathy · Aware of challenges
🐝 A buzzing hive of people and a breezy corridor!

During the long break, Yu and Jun went to the school cooperative to buy milk with their spare change. As soon as they reached the door, Yu froze—it was packed with thirty or forty students, all shouting at the top of their lungs: "I want tea eggs! I want bread!" The cash register beeped, steam billowed out. The various sounds and smells mingled together, like thousands of bees buzzing in Yu's head! Yu's face turned pale, and he stood rooted to the spot. Seeing Yu's blank stare, Jun immediately remembered the "off-site recharging method" taught in class. Jun gently pulled Yu's hand and led him to the camphor tree-lined corridor outside the cooperative: "Yu, let's enjoy the breeze under the trees and take three deep breaths!" In the quiet shade, with the gentle breeze, Yu's mental alarm finally subsided.

🤔 Class discussion guidance questions:When you feel dizzy and nauseous in a crowded, noisy, and smelly place, how do you recharge yourself?
🎭 Four character situation mini theater 🦁Yu 🐻Jun 🐼He 🦊Jia full-staff drill
🎬 Today's drill scenario:The cooperative is bustling and stuffy. The four little heroes practice identifying sensory overload and remind each other to recharge in a ventilated area!
🦁 Yu Calm and self-disciplined Yu
🎬 Action:When you feel your brain is about to shut down, make a pause gesture to Jun, turn around and walk to the camphor tree, close your eyes and take a deep breath.
"Huh~ The sound inside is too loud. My battery is almost out of power. I want to charge it under the tree for three minutes!" ”
💡 Tips:Guide Yu to independently initiate a preventive exit strategy before collapse.
🐻 Jun A courageous and responsible young man
🎬 Action:Instead of pushing and shoving through the crowd, they proactively accompanied Yu to the corridor and helped carry the milk bottle.
"Don't worry, Yu, I'll be with you outside!" We will buy it again when there are fewer people in the cooperative! ”
💡 Tips:Guide people to develop positive empathy that enthusiastically protects their weaker peers.
🐼 He Gentle and considerate little He
🎬 Action:Wipe the sweat from your forehead with a handkerchief, take a deep breath of fresh air in a well-ventilated area, and relax.
"The wind outside is so cool!"My brain is no longer knotted, and I have strength again!”
💡 Tips:Help He experience the help of sensory stress reduction on physiological balance.
🦊 Jia Enthusiastic and rule-abiding Jia
🎬 Action:Confirm that the surrounding environment is safe and free of obstacles, and use your watch to time three minutes to remind everyone of the break time.
"The three-minute charging timer begins!"Everyone close your eyes and wait for the beep before we go!”
💡 Tips:Guidingjia uses time structuring tools to help the team settle down physically and mentally.

Notice overload signals such as a buzzing brain, dizziness, and chest tightness.
2

3
Step back into a breezy corridor or a quiet corner and take three deep breaths.

🕶️ Soft Light Visual Protection Net
🏷️ Inspiration Library Special Topic 1: Sensory Regulation and Sensory Adaptation 📌 Field:⚡ Sensory Modulation
🎖️ Today’s Badge: Soft Light Adjustment Guardian

🔦 Bright Lights: Asking for Help and Adjusting the Room

🎯 Summary of core objectives:Strong fluorescent light flickering or intense afternoon sunlight can easily cause eye strain, migraines, and irritability in autistic children. Teachers should gently and politely ask children to turn off a light or gently close the blinds to create a visually friendly environment.

📖 Classroom situation adventure story island and questions Arouse empathy · Aware of challenges
☀️ The bright reflection on the blackboard contrasts beautifully with the soft beige curtains!

At 2 PM, during math class, the blazing afternoon sun shone directly into the special education classroom's blackboard! The blinding white light created a large reflection on the blackboard, so bright it was difficult to open one's eyes. Jia, sitting in the first row, squinted, her brows furrowed, her eyes stinging and watering, making it impossible to see the questions. Jia wanted to slam her hand on the desk and shout, "It's too bright! It's so annoying!" But then she remembered the "soft light communication method" her teacher had taught her. Jia stood up, placed her hands flat, and politely said, "Teacher, there's a glare from the sun on the blackboard, it's hurting my eyes. Could I please draw the beige curtains halfway?" The teacher praised, "Jia, that's excellent! Please go and draw the curtains!" When the soft beige curtains were drawn, the blinding white light transformed into a warm, soft glow, making it much more comfortable for everyone to see the blackboard!

🤔 Class discussion guidance questions:When the sunlight is too bright or the lighting gives you a headache, will yelling and shouting solve the problem? How can we get everyone to work together to create comfortable lighting?
🎭 Four character situation mini theater 🦁Yu 🐻Jun 🐼He 🦊Jia full-staff drill
🎬 Today's drill scenario:In the afternoon, the direct sunlight on the blackboard caused strong glare. The four little heroes practiced politely expressing their needs and worked together to adjust the classroom lighting!
🦁 Yu Calm and self-disciplined Yu
🎬 Action:If you feel a stinging sensation in your eyes from a reflection, gently cover your brow bone with your hand and quietly raise your hand to wait for your turn to speak.
"Tell the teacher, I can't see the words clearly due to the reflection in the middle of the blackboard. I want to see it from another angle."”
💡 Tips:Guide Yu to actively adjust the viewing angle and restrain the frustration and anxiety caused by unclear vision.
🐻 Jun A courageous and responsible young man
🎬 Action:Walk lightly to the window and slowly pull the curtain cord with both hands, without pulling hard.
"Don't worry, Jia, I'm strong, I'll help pull the curtains neatly so that they won't be dazzling!" ”
💡 Tips:Guide students to turn their abundant energy into concrete actions that serve the class.
🐼 He Gentle and considerate little He
🎬 Action:Rub your eyes in soft light, smile, and pick up a pencil to highlight key points in your textbook.
"After closing the curtains, the numbers on the blackboard can be seen clearly. Thank you everyone! ”
💡 Tips:Help He experience the positive impact of a friendly environment on learning concentration.
🦊 Jia Enthusiastic and rule-abiding Jia
🎬 Action:Politely raise your hand and stand up, and clearly and loudly state the specific situation where the light is too glaring.
"Teacher, the blackboard will reflect when the sun shines directly on it. Can we close half of the curtains?"”
💡 Tips:Guide Jia to use clear spoken language to directly express specific environmental adjustment demands.

🦷 Health Checkups: Preparing for New People and Equipment

🎯 Summary of core objectives:Special education students often resist and scream when faced with metal mouth mirrors, vision hoods, and white-coated medical staff during school health checks due to the unknown and fear of touch. Through role-playing scenarios to see the examination steps, coupled with the "Big Mouth Ah~ Three Seconds" exercise, they can overcome their fear of medical procedures.

📖 Classroom situation adventure story island and questions Arouse empathy · Aware of challenges
🐊 A baby crocodile with its mouth wide open and a magical little silver mirror!

Today, the activity center set up rows of health check stations, with dentists in white coats holding long, thin, shiny metal mirrors. When it was the special education class's turn to line up, He was so frightened by the metal instruments that tears streamed down his face. He covered his mouth tightly with his hands and hid behind the teacher, refusing to sit in the swivel chair. The teacher took out a small crocodile doll and demonstrated with a smile: "He, look, the little crocodile is going to look in the mirror to check its teeth! Open your mouth wide and say: Ah—one, two, three!" The dentist gently squatted down and lightly touched the back of He's hand with the round metal mirror: "Look, this is just a small flashlight mirror to illuminate the teeth. It's cool and doesn't hurt at all!" He touched the back of his hand, took a deep breath, sat in the chair, and boldly opened his mouth, saying: "Ah—!" The dentist praised: "Such clean teeth! It only took three seconds!" He happily received a brave sticker!

🤔 Class discussion guidance questions:If you keep your mouth tightly shut and cry during a health check, will the doctor still be able to examine you? What can you do to make yourself brave when you're scared?
🎭 Four character situation mini theater 🦁Yu 🐻Jun 🐼He 🦊Jia full-staff drill
🎬 Today's drill scenario:While waiting in line for a routine health check at school, four little heroes practice cooperating with the dentist to open their mouths and overcome their fear!
🦁 Yu Calm and self-disciplined Yu
🎬 Action:Sit on the examination chair, look at the star stickers on the ceiling, open your mouth wide and hold for three seconds without moving.
"I looked at the ceiling and counted one, two, three. Just touch the small metal mirror and it was fine. It really didn't hurt at all! ”
💡 Tips:Guide Yu to use the visual focus transfer method to overcome the fear of touching instruments.
🐻 Jun A courageous and responsible young man
🎬 Action:Place both hands neatly on your knees, cooperate fully with the vision check, and use the baton to accurately indicate the direction of E.
"The gap is facing up!"The gap faces left! My visual acuity is 1.0 in both eyes. I have superhuman vision!”
💡 Tips:Guide the patient to transform his competitive spirit into a positive performance of conscientiously cooperating with the physical examination.
🐼 He Gentle and considerate little He
🎬 Action:Hold the teacher's hand and sit on the chair. Bravely open your mouth. After the examination, bow to the dentist and say thank you.
"Ah - I did it!" I take good care of my teeth. The doctor said I don’t have any cavities! ”
💡 Tips:Help He overcome medical anxiety and build self-confidence in physical care.
🦊 Jia Enthusiastic and rule-abiding Jia
🎬 Action:Help by holding everyone's health check record form, reading out the students' names in order, and assisting with the queuing process.
"The next one is Yu!"Everyone stands in one square, take the health check form and don’t lose it!”
💡 Tips:Guide Jia to undertake specific class administrative tasks and maintain smooth order in the team.

Use the mantra "open your mouth wide, count to one, two, three, and take the sticker home" to simplify process memory.
🔹 Students with Emotional Disorders (EBD)
It is allowed to hold a familiar comfort doll or parent photo in your hand during the examination to increase the sense of security.

🎖️ Today’s Badge: Rainy Day Vitality Stretch Officer

🌧️ Rainy-Day PE: Stretching Indoors

🎯 Summary of core objectives:The long-awaited physical education class on the playground was forced to be moved indoors due to torrential rain. Hyperactive and emotionally unstable students often became agitated and ran away because their kinetic energy could not be released. The students were taught to use chair squats, stretching exercises, and resistance bands in the classroom to regulate their proprioception and stabilize their physical and mental energy.

📖 Classroom situation adventure story island and questions Arouse empathy · Aware of challenges
☔ A large puddle on the playground and a small gymnastics routine in the classroom!

The fourth period was everyone's most anticipated PE class. Everyone changed into their sneakers, ready to go to the playground to play soccer! Suddenly, thunder rumbled, followed by a torrential downpour, turning the playground into a muddy mess of puddles. The PE teacher walked into the classroom and announced, "It's raining too hard today, so we'll study in the classroom and watch a soccer game video instead." Hearing that they couldn't go to the playground, Jun angrily kicked over his chair: "Damn this awful rain! I've been preparing to play soccer all week, I don't care, I want to go outside and run!" He was as angry as a popcorn about to explode. The teacher came over, righted the chair, and said with a smile, "If we can't run on the playground, then we'll have an 'Indoor Spy Stretching Challenge' in the classroom!" The teacher led everyone in "chair-suspended squats," "wall push-ups," and "turtle-like static core exercises." After ten minutes, Jun was working up a good sweat, and all his frustration had vanished: "Wow! Wall push-ups and squats are even more fun than playing soccer!"

🤔 Class discussion guidance questions:When it's raining heavily and we can't run on the playground, can kicking over a classroom chair stop the rain? What indoor activities can we use our strength in the right way?
🎭 Four character situation mini theater 🦁Yu 🐻Jun 🐼He 🦊Jia full-staff drill
🎬 Today's drill scenario:Heavy rain caused PE class to be moved to the classroom. Four little heroes practiced controlling their tempers and working together to do indoor core stretches!
🦁 Yu Calm and self-disciplined Yu
🎬 Action:Feeling uneasy about the sudden change in the class schedule? Look at the wall-pushing picture card and push the wall with both hands for ten seconds to relieve anxiety.
"Pushing against the solid wall, my hands feel very powerful and I don't feel panic anymore!"”
💡 Tips:Guiding Yu calms the anxiety of sudden stroke changes through heavy resistance proprioceptive input.
🐻 Jun A courageous and responsible young man
🎬 Action:Right the chair that was kicked over, and follow the teacher to do double squats, turning excess energy into healthy sweat.
"Breathe in!"Squatting five times will really make you sweat! I no longer kick the chair, I am now a squat strongman!”
💡 Tips:Help Jun to transform destructive impulses into positive, high-intensity physical outlets.
🐼 He Gentle and considerate little He
🎬 Action:Sit on a chair and stretch your spine upwards with both hands, like a sapling growing in the rain, with a joyful expression.
"It's so comfortable to do stretching exercises in the classroom on a rainy day!"The muscles and bones are stretched and the whole person is energetic!”
💡 Tips:Help He experience the benefits of gentle stretching for circulation and focus.
🦊 Jia Enthusiastic and rule-abiding Jia
🎬 Action:Stand in front of the podium and count the beats: "One, two, three, four; two, two, three, four," leading all students to perform the movements in unison.
"Preparation - Pushing the wall starts in ten seconds!" One, two, three... everyone moved very neatly! ”
💡 Tips:Guiding Jia serves as the command commander and brings the sense of structural rhythm into class activities.

🎯 Super power move visual chart card ⭐ Three indoor stretching moves for rainy days
1
Accept the natural limitations of rainy weather, take a deep breath and tell yourself: "It's okay, it's fun indoors too."
2
Push firmly against a solid wall with both hands, elbows slightly bent, for ten seconds to release mental stress
3
Perform five chair squats with both feet on the ground to give your muscles a comfortable workout.

Draw the actions of "Push the wall/Chair Squat/Towel Stretch" into a large picture card and paste it on the blackboard.
🔹 Students with Emotional Disorders (EBD)
Provide high-resistance elastic bands or medicine ball push and push music to release intense emotions through the proprioception of heavy resistance.

🎾 Two-way conversational ball throwing and catching
🏷️ Inspiration Library Topic 2: Pragmatic Communication and Implicit Social Codes 📌 Field:🗣️ Pragmatic communication
🎖️ Today’s badge: Throwing, catching and chatting master

🦖 Sharing My Favorite Topic: Taking Turns in Conversation

🎯 Summary of core objectives:Autistic children often launch into lengthy monologues about specific interests (dinosaurs, bus routes, Pokémon), ignoring their peers who are already lost in thought or wanting to leave. Teach them to use the "three-sentence pause" technique and proactively throw the conversation back to them: "So, what do you like?"

📖 Classroom situation adventure story island and questions Arouse empathy · Aware of challenges
⚾ The baseball flying non-stop and the ball being passed back and forth!

Ten minutes into the break, Yu grabbed Jun and excitedly launched into a rapid-fire lecture: "Did you know that Charizard has two Mega Evolutions? The X-type is Dragon and Fire, with incredibly high attack power... and Mewtwo's gene arrangement..." Yu talked for eight minutes straight without stopping, gesturing excitedly with his hands. Standing opposite him, Jun's eyes were already drifting towards the playground, his feet involuntarily taking steps backward, muttering, "Yu, I need to go to the bathroom..." But Yu didn't hear him at all, continuing his endless chatter. Just then, Jia gently patted Yu's shoulder and handed him a tennis ball: "Yu, chatting is like passing a ball. If you keep throwing and not letting others catch, their arms will get sore!" Yu paused, seeing Jun's anxious look, and quickly slammed on the brakes: "Ah! Sorry, Jun, I talked too much! What's your favorite game? You throw the ball!" Jun smiled: "I like dodgeball, let's go after school!"

🤔 Class discussion guidance questions:When you keep talking about your favorite things and don't let anyone else speak, how will the other person feel? How can we create a "give and take" atmosphere in conversation?
🎭 Four character situation mini theater 🦁Yu 🐻Jun 🐼He 🦊Jia full-staff drill
🎬 Today's drill scenario:After class, share your favorite toys or cartoons. The four little heroes practice restraining their monologues, asking each other questions, and listening to each other!
🦁 Yu Calm and self-disciplined Yu
🎬 Action:After saying your two favorite sentences from the dinosaur encyclopedia, pause and gesture towards Jun.
"This is my favorite Triceratops!" Now that I’ve finished talking, it’s your turn to be Xiaojiu. What’s your favorite animal? ”
💡 Tips:Guide Yu to self-monitor the conversation volume and proactively ask questions when special interests are stimulated.
🐻 Jun A courageous and responsible young man
🎬 Action:Make a catching motion with both hands, look at Yu, and continue the conversation with a smile.
"I caught the good ball!" My favorite is the cheetah because it can run as fast as me! ”
💡 Tips:The guidance department actively responds to peer dialogue and establishes successful experiences in two-way communication.
🐼 He Gentle and considerate little He
🎬 Action:Listen attentively to the two people talking, nod and smile to encourage your peers.
"The Triceratops is strong, the cheetah runs fast, your favorite animals are all so unique!"”
💡 Tips:Guidance and practice in the harmonious role of listening and connected dialogue.
🦊 Jia Enthusiastic and rule-abiding Jia
🎬 Action:Holding a conversation timer hourglass in his hand, he watches everyone take turns speaking with a focused expression.
"Everyone takes turns talking for one minute, and everyone has something to say. This time the chat, passing and receiving was a great success!"”
💡 Tips:Guide Jia to maintain an equal voice mechanism through time and rule structures.

🎯 Super power move visual chart card ⭐ Three steps to conversational ball toss and catch
1
Realizing he had already uttered three sentences in a row, he immediately put the brakes on his brain.
2
Observe whether the other person's eyes are looking at you, or if they are already looking around and trying to leave.
3
Throw the conversation ball to the other person: "And what about you? What do you like best?" And listen attentively.
🎯 IEP Quantitative Goals & Putt Collaboration & Family Life Behavioral classification tripartite connection
🎯 IEP observable quantitative goals:In a free dialogue situation, be able to restrain continuous monologues and actively ask open-ended questions to guide peers to speak within 3 sentences, with an achievement rate of more than 80%.
🏫 Post-it notes on integration tips for regular class instructors:
A timing hourglass can be given during group chats in ordinary classes (each person takes a turn for 1 minute) to help autistic students visualize the length of their speeches.
🏠 Home Practice Check-In:
Practice the "throwing and catching conversation method" when chatting with your family. After speaking three sentences, ask your mother what interesting things happened today!

🔹 Students with Learning Disabilities (LD)
Utilize physical tennis props to pass between two people, whoever has the ball speaks.
🔹 Students with Emotional Disorders (EBD)
When peers show boredom or want to leave, practice accepting "other people have different interests" and not get angry or angry.

🧠 Filtered Gum for Words
🏷️ Inspiration Library Topic 2: Pragmatic Communication and Implicit Social Codes 📌 Field:🗣️ Pragmatic communication
🎖️ Today’s Badge: Thoughtful and Speaking Guardian Officer

🤐 Honest and Kind: Thinking Before Speaking

🎯 Summary of core objectives:Special education children often suffer from interpersonal disasters due to their blunt cognition, saying "your new hair style is ugly" or "your lunch box smells so bad" in public. Guide school children to establish a "thinking filter", distinguish between "objective facts" and "hurtful comments", and learn to chew their brains three times before speaking.

📖 Classroom situation adventure story island and questions Arouse empathy · Aware of challenges
🍋 Tart lemon candy and sweet marshmallows!

He got a new haircut today, with short bangs. She walked into the classroom a little shyly. As soon as Xiaozuo saw it, he immediately pointed at He's head and laughed loudly and shouted: "Hahaha!"He, your head looks like it has been chewed by a dog. It’s so ugly!"When He heard this, his whole face turned pale instantly, tears welled up in his eyes, and he lay on the table with his head down and cried. The teacher came over and gently invited Jia to the side: "Xiaojiu, your words are like a sour lemon piercing He's heart." Even if you think your hairstyle is different, calling someone "so ugly" in public will make them very sad. ” The teacher taught everyone the formula for chewing “brain filter gum”: “Is this sentence true? Is it necessary to say this? Does it make you sad to hear this? "Xiaojiu looked at the sobbing He and felt very guilty. He stepped forward and bowed sincerely: "He, I'm sorry, I shouldn't have laughed at your hair. It looks refreshing if you cut it short. Please forgive me! ”

🤔 Class discussion guidance questions:When you see a classmate wearing new clothes or having a new haircut, if you just shout "so ugly", how will the other person feel? What trouble can you avoid by chewing three times in your brain before you want to speak?
🎭 Four character situation mini theater 🦁Yu 🐻Jun 🐼He 🦊Jia full-staff drill
🎬 Today's drill scenario:A classmate got new glasses or a new hairstyle. The four little heroes practice activating their verbal filters to avoid saying hurtful things!
🦁 Yu Calm and self-disciplined Yu
🎬 Action:Seeing He's new hairstyle, you feel a little uncomfortable. You think about it for three seconds and don't blurt out any strange comments.
"He, you cut your hair short!" It must be so cool to have physical education class in the summer! ”
💡 Tips:Guide Yu to turn observed facts into practical function-oriented positive responses.
🐻 Jun A courageous and responsible young man
🎬 Action:Immediately stop making a mocking face, put your hands behind your back, and sincerely apologize to the peer who was hurt.
"I've chewed the brain gum!" I'm sorry He, I shouldn't criticize your hair casually! ”
💡 Tips:Guide people to recognize the hurtful nature of words and implement immediate oral apology repairs.
🐼 He Gentle and considerate little He
🎬 Action:Wipe away your tears with a handkerchief, feel the sincere apology from your peers, and raise your head to smile bravely.
"Thank you everyone, actually I was a little uncomfortable at first, but now I feel very relaxed!”
💡 Tips:Guiding and rebuilding body image and mental resilience from peer feedback.
🦊 Jia Enthusiastic and rule-abiding Jia
🎬 Action:Hold up the Classroom Consideration Rules card to remind everyone to maintain respect for and appreciation of diversity.
"Everyone has the freedom to change their hairstyle!"Praise and respect are the first rules in our classroom!”
💡 Tips:Guide and maintain a psychologically safe atmosphere in the class with empathy.

🎯 Super power move visual chart card ⭐ Brain Chew Three Times Filtering Method
1
Perceived urge to blurt out comments about peers' appearance, lunch, or clothing
2
Chew the gum three times in your mind and ask yourself: "Does this sentence make you want to cry?"”
3
Take the hurtful thorn back into your belly and replace it with praise or keep polite and quiet
🎯 IEP Quantitative Goals & Putt Collaboration & Family Life Behavioral classification tripartite connection
🎯 IEP observable quantitative goals:When faced with peers' appearance, works or personal characteristics, they can restrain themselves from making inappropriate direct comments, use neutral or positive language to interact, and do not make fun of them in public. The achievement rate is above 85%.
🏫 Post-it notes on integration tips for regular class instructors:
Regular class tutors should establish the routine of "zero appearance teasing in class" to guide children to see the uniqueness and dignity of each person.
🏠 Home Practice Check-In:
After returning home from school, show your parents how to🧠 Word Filter Chewing Gum" and give warm high fives to your family!
🧩 Individualized differentiated support (support scaffolding for students with special needs) UDL multiple representation and participation
🔹 Students with autism spectrum disorder (ASD)
Show the "traffic light filter list": red light (hurtful appearance evaluation), no speaking, yellow light (personal feelings), whisper in private, green light (praise and gratitude), speak loudly.
🔹 Students with Learning Disabilities (LD)
Use the image of "a lotus flower spits out of your mouth to speak good words, and a poisonous snake spits out of your mouth to speak bad words" to metaphorize the consequences of speaking.
🔹 Students with Emotional Disorders (EBD)
Practice pressing your tongue against the roof of your mouth for three seconds to force your brain to calm down before you laugh or blurt it out.

🔍 Voice and Tone Decoding Mirror
🏷️ Inspiration Library Topic 2: Pragmatic Communication and Implicit Social Codes 📌 Field:🗣️ Pragmatic communication
🎖️ Today’s Badge: Mind Decoding Detective

🎭 Joking or Teasing? Listening for Tone and Intent

🎯 Summary of core objectives:Autistic schoolchildren are often unable to recognize irony, joking or ridicule in the tone of voice, and are prone to take a friend's well-intentioned jokes as an attack and punch them, or take malicious ridicule seriously. Teach people how to recognize good-natured jokes by "smiling at the corner of the mouth/gentle eyes/close to the body".

📖 Classroom situation adventure story island and questions Arouse empathy · Aware of challenges
🎭 Crooked smile and gentle eyes!

When playing volleyball after class, Yu accidentally missed the ball while serving, and the ball rolled gently to Jia's feet. Jia picked up the ball and said with a smile, "Wow!" Yu, your ball hits a home run, fly to the moon! ” Several classmates around him started laughing. Yu's face turned red, and he clenched his fists tightly, shouting: "Why are you laughing at me!"Are you laughing at my stupidity?"Raise your hands to grab the ball."The teacher came over and gently held Yu's shoulders: "Yu, wait!"Please look at Jia's eyes - is she smiling and looking at you tenderly, or is she looking at you sideways? Did she hide the ball from you, or did she hand it to you with both hands?"Yu was stunned for a moment and saw Jia holding the ball in both hands with friendly eyes. Jia quickly said, "I'm sorry, Yu. I was just joking. I'm not saying you are stupid. You are really strong!" "Yu unclenched his fist: "So you were playing with me, I thought you were scolding me..."

🤔 Class discussion guidance questions:When someone says something to you and laughs, how do you tell whether he is having fun with you or laughing at you maliciously?
🎭 Four character situation mini theater 🦁Yu 🐻Jun 🐼He 🦊Jia full-staff drill
🎬 Today's drill scenario:A colleague's humorous remark on the court leads to a misunderstanding. The four little heroes practice recognizing intonation clues and clearly clarifying the intention!
🦁 Yu Calm and self-disciplined Yu
🎬 Action:If you notice your heart racing and you want to clench your fist, take a deep breath, look at the other person's face, and ask to confirm their intention.
"Jia, you just laughed and said the moon home run. Are you kidding me or laughing at me?"”
💡 Tips:Guide Yu to actively seek verification through spoken language instead of direct physical attacks.
🐻 Jun A courageous and responsible young man
🎬 Action:Assist in observing the situation from the sidelines, and pat Yu on the shoulder to act as a peace mediator.
"Yu, relax!" Jia is praising you for your strength. Our volleyball team needs your strong serve! ”
💡 Tips:Guide people to use their sense of justice to resolve interpersonal misunderstandings.
🐼 He Gentle and considerate little He
🎬 Action:Place the volleyball back into Yu's hands with both hands, with sincere eyes and a gentle, comforting tone.
"Yu is fine, everyone is on the same team, let's catch the ball together!" ”
💡 Tips:Help He use friendly body movements to resolve tense confrontations.
🦊 Jia Enthusiastic and rule-abiding Jia
🎬 Action:Put your hands together to express apology, immediately explain the original meaning of your humor, and eliminate your peers' unease.
"Yu, I'm sorry!" I spoke too exaggeratedly and misunderstood you. I really think you are very strong and handsome! ”
💡 Tips:Guide Jia to notice the peculiarities of literal interpretation of words by autistic peers and provide timely clarification.

1
When you notice the anger that hardens your fist, stop for three seconds.
2
Observe the other person’s eyes (gentle gaze) and corners of the mouth (friendly smile)
3
When unsure, ask directly: "Are you kidding me?"”
🎯 IEP Quantitative Goals & Putt Collaboration & Family Life Behavioral classification tripartite connection
🎯 IEP observable quantitative goals:When peers engage in verbal humor or joking, they can observe non-verbal clues (expressions, eyes) and correctly interpret intentions without misjudgment of aggressive behavior. The achievement rate is above 85%.
🏫 Post-it notes on integration tips for regular class instructors:
Students in regular classes are reminded to keep their spoken language as direct and clear as possible when interacting with children with autism, and avoid excessive metaphors or irony.
🏠 Home Practice Check-In:
After returning home from school, show your parents how to🔍 Voice and Intonation Decoding Mirror" and give warm high fives to your family!
🧩 Individualized differentiated support (support scaffolding for students with special needs) UDL multiple representation and participation
🔹 Students with autism spectrum disorder (ASD)
Provide a "good-natured joking vs. malicious teasing" comparison checklist: good-natured (eye gaze, sharing toys, relaxed expression); malicious (rolling eyes, pushing, calling ugly nicknames).
🔹 Students with Learning Disabilities (LD)
Use puppetry to perform two different intonations (gentle and brisk vs. harsh), so that school children can identify the difference with their ears.
🔹 Students with Emotional Disorders (EBD)
Before you get angry and take action, ask the other person: "Are you kidding me, or are you serious?"” Clarify the intention.

🔒 Privacy Boundary Security Lock
🏷️ Inspiration Library Topic 2: Pragmatic Communication and Implicit Social Codes 📌 Field:🗣️ Pragmatic communication
🎖️ Today’s Badge: Patron Saint of Personal Privacy

📱 Respecting Privacy: Ask Before Looking

🎯 Summary of core objectives:Special education children often unzip their peers' schoolbags and read the red letters in their contact books or diaries at will due to their strong curiosity or lack of concept of property rights and privacy boundaries, causing strong resentment among their peers. Guide school children to establish safe boundaries where "other people's personal belongings will never be touched".

📖 Classroom situation adventure story island and questions Arouse empathy · Aware of challenges
🎒 The tightly closed zipper and the little fox’s secret notes!

After class, Jia went to the bathroom. Her pink schoolbag was placed on the chair. The zipper was slightly opened, revealing a beautiful secret diary with a golden unicorn on the cover. When Xiaoji passed by, he became very curious and thought to himself: "Wow!" It's a unicorn diary. I wonder what interesting things are written in it? ” Xiaojiu couldn't help but reached out and unzipped the zipper, took out the diary and flipped through it. At this time, Jia walked into the classroom and saw that her diary was opened. She was so angry that she burst into tears. She screamed and rushed forward and pushed Jia away: "Why are you peeking at my things!" Thief! What a nuisance! "The teacher came over seriously: "Xiaojiu, your schoolbag and diary are everyone's private castle. Opening other people's schoolbags or looking through diaries without permission is a very disrespectful and intrusive act! "When Jia saw Jia crying so sadly, she lowered her head in shame. She put the diary back into her school bag and zipped it up with both hands: "I'm sorry, Jia, I'm too curious. I promise never to rummage through other people's things again!"”

🤔 Class discussion guidance questions:When you really want to see something interesting in your classmate’s schoolbag, can you just take it out and look through it? Why is respecting other people’s privacy the most important boundary in making friends?
🎭 Four character situation mini theater 🦁Yu 🐻Jun 🐼He 🦊Jia full-staff drill
🎬 Today's drill scenario:Seeing a beautiful notebook peeking out of a classmate's backpack, the four little heroes practice activating the privacy lock and restraining their voyeuristic desires!
🦁 Yu Calm and self-disciplined Yu
🎬 Action:If you see an open communication book on a classmate's desk, put your hands in your pockets and take a step back to avoid peeking.
"That's Jia's private contact book. I can't read it. I want to protect my friend's privacy castle!" ”
💡 Tips:Guide Yu to establish a clear concept of personal and spatial privacy boundaries.
🐻 Jun A courageous and responsible young man
🎬 Action:Resist the urge to touch with your hands, put your palms together and bow deeply to Jia to express your apology and promise.
"I'm sorry Jia!"I will never touch the zipper of your schoolbag in the future. I will be a good friend who keeps his word!”
💡 Tips:Guide people to experience the consequences of violating others' boundaries and implement their commitment to respecting boundaries.
🐼 He Gentle and considerate little He
🎬 Action:Gently walk over and help Jia zip up her schoolbag, then hand her a tissue to comfort her crying classmate.
"Don't cry, Jia. The zipper of your schoolbag is tightened. Your little secrets are safe!" ”
💡 Tips:Help He support peers with specific maintenance behaviors.
🦊 Jia Enthusiastic and rule-abiding Jia
🎬 Action:Put away your notebook, wipe away your tears, and accept Jun's apology gracefully.
"Thank you for apologizing to me. As long as you promise to ask me first in the future, we will still be good friends!" ”
💡 Tips:After establishing the boundaries of personal privacy, Guidance shows tolerance and the mind to repair relationships.

1
Do not open other people's bag zippers or drawers casually
2
Do not read other people’s contact book comments and personal diaries
3
When you are curious and want to borrow something, you must first look into the other person's eyes and say, "Can I see it?"”

After returning home from school, show your parents how to🔒 Privacy Boundary Security Lock" and give a warm high-five to your family!

Establish clear property rights rules: "schoolbags, pencil cases, contact books, pockets = private castles, I can't touch them unless you ask me to borrow them."
🔹 Students with Learning Disabilities (LD)
Hang a "personal name tag" on the bag handle of each student in the class to strengthen the awareness of ownership.
🔹 Students with Emotional Disorders (EBD)
Transform curiosity into a positive spoken request: "Your notebook is so beautiful. Can you lend it to me to see the cover after class?"

🌫️ Classroom Weather Barometer
🏷️ Inspiration Library Topic 2: Pragmatic Communication and Implicit Social Codes 📌 Field:🗣️ Pragmatic communication
🎖️ Today’s badge: Master of understanding the air

🤫 Noticing the Setting and Communicating a Need for a Break or Quiet Self Regulation

🎯 Summary of core objectives:During a quiet reading period or rest time, a learner may use sounds or repeated speech to regulate. Preview the setting and offer ways to communicate a need for movement, a quieter activity or a break.

📖 Classroom situation adventure story island and questions Arouse empathy · Aware of challenges
📺 The big TV in your mouth and the quiet lunch break bell!

At 12:30 noon, the soft lunch break bell rang on the campus. The whole class lay down on the table and closed their eyes to sleep. The whole classroom was so quiet that you could hear a pin drop. Yu was lying on the table, but his head was like a movie projector, constantly replaying the Superman cartoon he watched last night! Yu couldn't help but make a sharp dubbing sound with his mouth: "Boom——!"Light wave emission! pound! pound! Defeat the bad guys!"The classmates lying next to them were woken up one by one, holding their heads in annoyance: "Yu is so noisy! Do you want to sleep or not?"The teacher walked gently to Yu, took out a "Quiet Kitty Lying Card" and placed it on the corner of the table: "Yu, look up and look around - what is the color of the air in the class now? Everyone is closing their eyes to rest. At this time, we have to turn off the big TV in our mouths and switch to brain silent mode to think about Superman!"When Yu saw everyone's tired faces, he quickly shut his mouth. He closed his eyes and watched Superman quietly in his head, and everyone fell asleep comfortably!

🤔 Class discussion guidance questions:When people nearby are resting or reading, what can you notice about the setting and how could you ask for support?
🎭 Four character situation mini theater 🦁Yu 🐻Jun 🐼He 🦊Jia full-staff drill
🎬 Today's drill scenario:During lunch break and self-study, in a quiet environment, the four little heroes practiced recognizing the group atmosphere and switching to mental silence mode!
🦁 Yu Calm and self-disciplined Yu
🎬 Action:When you realize you have the urge to recite your lines, take a deep breath, close your mouth tightly, and rest your head on the table with your eyes closed.
"It's lunch break now, everyone is sleeping, I want to watch Superman with my brain muted, so as not to disturb everyone!"”
💡 Tips:Guide Yu to convert spoken vocalizations into internal language representations, improving situational acuity.
🐻 Jun A courageous and responsible young man
🎬 Action:Gently tuck your feet back into place, which are about to shake and kick the table, and lie down properly with your eyes closed.
"I also want to understand the air!" The whole class was sleeping, so I lay down quietly and acted like a self-disciplined gentleman! ”
💡 Tips:Guide and coordinate with the group rhythm to stabilize the physical and mental state.
🐼 He Gentle and considerate little He
🎬 Action:Gently draw the curtains to block out the light, quietly walk back to your seat and lie down without making a sound.
"Walk gently, lie down slowly, everyone sleeps soundly, the classroom is so warm!" ”
💡 Tips:Help He maintain the self-disciplined action habits of a peaceful class environment.
🦊 Jia Enthusiastic and rule-abiding Jia
🎬 Action:Hang a "Lunch Break Silence Red Light" sign in front of the podium to remind the whole class to enter deep rest mode.
"It's charging time for the whole class. Please turn down the generator and enjoy the quiet time!"”
💡 Tips:Guide Jia to use visual symbols to implement group situational routines.

🙆 The art of sincere listening and nodding.
🏷️ Inspiration Library Topic 2: Pragmatic Communication and Implicit Social Codes 📌 Field:🗣️ Pragmatic communication
🎖️ Today’s Badge: Big Ears Listening Ambassador

👂 Showing I Am Listening: Attention and Body Language

🎯 Summary of core objectives:Special education students often turn their backs to others and fidget with their hands while listening to them, making it seem as if they are not listening at all. We teach them the "Three Treasures of Listening to Body Language": lean slightly forward, look at the other person's forehead, and nod gently after understanding each sentence.

📖 Classroom situation adventure story island and questions Arouse empathy · Aware of challenges
🗿 A wooden figure and a nodding sunflower!

Today, Jia excitedly shared with He the funny story she had about seeing five ducklings in the park yesterday: "He, look! The mother duck is leading her ducklings swimming in the water, and the last duckling almost slipped! It's so cute!" Although He didn't speak, her body was turned sideways to Jia, her eyes fixed on the eraser in her hand, motionless like a cold wooden statue. As Jia spoke, her voice grew softer and softer, and finally she lowered her head in frustration: "He, you weren't listening to me at all, were you? I'm so bored..." He hurriedly raised her head: "Yes! I was listening! You said five ducklings!" The teacher smiled and said: "He, your ears are listening, but your body is asleep! When others are speaking, our bodies should be like a sunflower, facing the sun, with our face towards the speaker. After understanding each sentence, nod slightly and say 'Yes! Really!', so that the other person can see your sincerity!" He immediately turned to look at Jia and nodded: "Jia, continue, did the duckling catch up with its mother later?" Jia's eyes lit up immediately!

🤔 Class discussion guidance questions:If a classmate keeps looking down at something and ignoring you while you're talking, would you want to continue talking to them? How can you use actions to let the other person know you're listening attentively?
🎭 Four character situation mini theater 🦁Yu 🐻Jun 🐼He 🦊Jia full-staff drill
🎬 Today's drill scenario:Partners share wonderful life experiences, and the four little heroes practice using body language to demonstrate sincere listening!
🦁 Yu Calm and self-disciplined Yu
🎬 Action:Put down the building blocks in your hand, turn your body towards Jia who is speaking, focus your eyes on Jia's brow, and nod gently.
"Jia, I'm listening!" Five little ducks are swimming in the water, what next? ”
💡 Tips:Guide Yu to overcome the eye avoidance habit and convey social goodwill with active orientation.
🐻 Jun A courageous and responsible young man
🎬 Action:Place both hands on your thighs without playing with the pen, lean your body slightly forward, and nod earnestly in agreement.
"Hmm!" I listened carefully! Did the little duck get home safely in the end? ”
💡 Tips:Help Jun to converge its restless limbs into a stable listening structure.
🐼 He Gentle and considerate little He
🎬 Action:Face Jia like a little sunflower, with a smile on your face, and listen attentively to every word your partner says.
"Now I have learned to be a sunflower!"Seeing you nodding, I know you are so happy today!”
💡 Tips:Help He externalize inner focus into warm limbs that make peers feel respected.
🦊 Jia Enthusiastic and rule-abiding Jia
🎬 Action:Seeing your peers looking at you so attentively and nodding makes you more vivid and confident in your sharing.
"You are all looking at me and listening to me. I feel so happy!" Finally, the mother duck rescued the duckling ashore! ”
💡 Tips:Guide Jia to experience the positive motivational feedback of being sincerely listened to by peers.

❓ When a Long Instruction Is Unclear - Ask the Teacher to Repeat the Second Step

🎯 Summary of core objectives:Faced with multiple instructions from the teacher, such as "Take out the blue notebook, turn to page 25, write the third question, and hand it in to the group leader," children with learning disabilities and autism often freeze up due to insufficient working memory. The teachers encourage students to raise their hands and ask to repeat the specified steps.

📖 Classroom situation adventure story island and questions Arouse empathy · Aware of challenges
🌪️ A long strip of paper flies away and a brave little hand is raised!

During science class, the teacher gave four instructions in one breath: "Please put away your pencil cases first, take out your yellow observation record books, turn to page eighteen, and draw today's bean sprouts. After you're done, give them to your group leader for stamping!" He sat in his seat, his mind a complete mess. He only remembered the first instruction about putting away his pencil cases; the rest was a jumbled mess! Watching his classmates take out their notebooks and start drawing, He's eyes welled up with tears. He sat there blankly, wanting to peek at the students next to him but too afraid to. The teacher came over and gently patted He's head: "He, it's normal not to understand or remember. Your brain needs time to process! Don't pretend you understand. Raise your hand and tell the teacher, 'Please tell me again what the second step is?'" He wiped away his tears, mustered his courage, and raised his right hand: "Teacher, I didn't hear the third step clearly. Who should I give it to after I finish drawing?" The teacher smiled and said, "That's a great question! Give it to your group leader for stamping!" He immediately took out his notebook and happily got to work!

🤔 Class discussion guidance questions:When the teacher explains many things that you don't understand or can't remember, is sitting in your seat and daydreaming helpful? How can you ask questions to understand the steps?
🎭 Four character situation mini theater 🦁Yu 🐻Jun 🐼He 🦊Jia full-staff drill
🎬 Today's drill scenario:When a multi-step task was explained in class and the student didn't understand, the four little heroes practiced raising their hands to confirm the steps without panicking!
🦁 Yu Calm and self-disciplined Yu
🎬 Action:Remember only the first two steps, take out your own sticky notes on the desk, raise your hand and ask the teacher to confirm the third step.
"Teacher, I have turned to page 18. Who should I hand over to the third step?"”
💡 Tips:Guide Yu to proactively use spoken language to check specific implementation details to reduce anxiety.
🐻 Jun A courageous and responsible young man
🎬 Action:Quickly put away the pencil case, and enthusiastically turn around to quietly remind He in the same group of the page number.
"Look, He, turn to this page to draw bean sprouts!" Let me open the book for you! ”
💡 Tips:Guide students to exert their enthusiasm for helping others and promote cooperative learning among peers.
🐼 He Gentle and considerate little He
🎬 Action:Bravely raise your right hand, with a firm look in your eyes, and clearly ask the teacher to repeat the instructions.
"Teacher, there are too many steps for me to remember. Could you please tell me the last step again?"”
💡 Tips:Help He overcome low self-esteem and shrinkage, and establish a sense of learning rights to actively ask for help.
🦊 Jia Enthusiastic and rule-abiding Jia
🎬 Action:Mark the three large numbers 1, 2, and 3 with a pattern on the blackboard with chalk to help the whole class visually memorize them.
"I wrote the steps on the blackboard!" The first step is to collect the pencil case, the second step is to draw beans, and the third step is to stamp it! ”
💡 Tips:Guidingjia benefits all students through the structured construction of the environment.

🔹 Students with Emotional Disorders (EBD)
Before being irritated and slapping the table because you cannot remember the instructions, guide them to raise their hands and take a deep breath to ask questions.

✏️ Writing Frustration: Put Down the Pencil and Take a Break

🎯 Summary of core objectives:Children with learning disabilities and motor coordination difficulties often tear their notebooks due to insufficient hand muscle strength, resulting in inconsistent handwriting, writing outside the lines, and excessive force when scratching. Guiding children to "put down the pen, rub their hands, and use patching stickers to repair the damage" helps build resilience.

📖 Classroom situation adventure story island and questions Arouse empathy · Aware of challenges
💣 Angry torn paper and magical transparent repair sticker!

During the vocabulary practice class, He held a thick triangular pencil tightly in his hand. Because my hand coordination is relatively weak, the thirteen horizontal lines on the right side of the word "listen" cannot fit into the square grid no matter how I write it, and it accidentally flies out of the grid! He picked up the eraser and rubbed hard, and the result was "Hiss——!" "With a sound, a big black hole was wiped out of the thin calligraphy pad! Looking at the broken notebook, He collapsed. Tears fell like broken pearls. He grabbed the entire calligraphy notebook and tried to tear it into pieces! The teacher's sharp eyesight and quick hands gently held He's wrist: "He, take a deep breath!"Your hands are too hard and too hard! Put down the pencil first and let’s do the “dough finger exercise”!” The teacher took out a small piece of green clay and asked He to squeeze it to relax his tense fingers. Then he took out a roll of transparent invisible tape and said, “It doesn’t matter if the paper is torn. We put on a piece of “Repair Velcro” and the hole will be repaired. Let’s write it again! ”He wiped away his tears, touched the flat tape, picked up the pen again, and wrote the words correctly one stroke at a time!

🤔 Class discussion guidance questions:When you can't write well or tear your notebook, will tearing the notebook make your handwriting neater? How can you relax when your hand is sore and you feel frustrated?
🎭 Four character situation mini theater 🦁Yu 🐻Jun 🐼He 🦊Jia full-staff drill
🎬 Today's drill scenario:Feeling frustrated and overwhelmed by erasing their pencils while writing, the four little heroes practice putting down their pencils, relieving the pressure on their fingers, and repairing the notebooks!
🦁 Yu Calm and self-disciplined Yu
🎬 Action:If you feel frustrated when writing outside the lines, take a deep breath, place the pen flat on the table, close your eyes, and count to five.
"It doesn't matter if the words exceed the grid, I will erase them and write slowly without losing my temper and dirtying the notebook!"”
💡 Tips:Guide Yu to overcome the compulsive fixation on perfect grid lines and accept reasonable stroke errors.
🐻 Jun A courageous and responsible young man
🎬 Action:When you see a fellow student about to tear up their notebook, immediately hand them transparent tape and encourage them with a firm tone.
"Don't tear it up, He!" It’s even more tiring to tear it up and have to rewrite it! Just put some tape on it and it will look like new! ”
💡 Tips:Guide people to experience impulse and turn it into timely positive persuasion from sympathetic peers.
🐼 He Gentle and considerate little He
🎬 Action:Put down the pencil, squeeze the soft clay in your palms to relax your fingers, and then apply the repair sticker.
"Phew~ My hands are relaxed!"The magic tape was put on, the hole was repaired, and I could write again!”
💡 Tips:Help He experience the sense of control after hand pressure reduction, and overcome frustration.
🦊 Jia Enthusiastic and rule-abiding Jia
🎬 Action:Gently place the pencil grip on He's pencil and adjust the angle of the pencil tip grip.
"With this soft pencil holder, your hands won't be so sore. Let's work hard together!"”
💡 Tips:Guide and use auxiliary teaching aids to provide partners with substantial support.

🤝 Read aloud a relay help card
🏷️ Inspiration Library Topic 3: Classroom Learning Frustrations and Homework Challenges 📌 Field:📝 Classroom learning
🎖️ Today’s badge: Little Warriors who read aloud with confidence

📖 Reading Aloud: Asking a Partner for Help

🎯 Summary of core objectives:Children with dyslexia often stumble and get stuck when taking turns reading aloud in class due to difficulties recognizing words, skipping lines, or breaking down characters, which can lead to laughter from peers and cause social trauma. Teaching methods can help resolve this by showing a "relay help card" and having group members read a sentence in turn.

📖 Classroom situation adventure story island and questions Arouse empathy · Aware of challenges
Dancing black ants and a warm relay baton!

In the Chinese class, the teacher asked the whole class to stand up and read a text aloud according to their seat numbers. When it was He's turn, she stood up with her textbook. In He's eyes, the Chinese characters on the textbook were like little black ants dancing in a crooked arrangement. He read the first three words: "Spring...day..." and then got stuck in front of the four words "breeze", and couldn't spell it out no matter how hard he spelled it. The whole class was quiet for five seconds. A few naughty students in the back row began to chuckle: "Why do you read so slowly?"”He's face instantly turned red like a ripe tomato, his legs were shaking, and tears were about to fall down. At this time, Jia, who was sitting in the front row, saw it and immediately raised the "green relay flag" in his hand, smiled and read aloud: "The breeze is blowing the green willow trees!"” The teacher immediately praised: “Jia did a great job! He also read very clearly!” With the partner relaying, He took a deep breath and finished the next sentence smoothly, and the whole class burst into warm applause!

🤔 Class discussion guidance questions:When you get stuck reading aloud on stage, what would you do if some classmates laughed? What's a good way to ask a good friend to help you finish?
🎭 Four character situation mini theater 🦁Yu 🐻Jun 🐼He 🦊Jia full-staff drill
🎬 Today's drill scenario:During class, students took turns reading the text and encountered difficulties with unfamiliar words. The four little heroes practiced a relay race to resolve the awkward situation!
🦁 Yu Calm and self-disciplined Yu
🎬 Action:While seated, point to each line of the text and follow along, silently encouraging He on stage as he reads.
"Come on He, I look at the words in the textbook and can help you read them at any time!" ”
💡 Tips:Guide Yu supports peer learning with visual tracking and focused companionship.
🐻 Jun A courageous and responsible young man
🎬 Action:If you hear someone laughing in the back row, immediately turn around and sternly stop them: "Don't laugh! Everyone is learning to read!"
"Everyone, be quiet!"He practices every day. It’s rude to laugh at others!”
💡 Tips:Guide students to use their sense of justice to stop bullying and maintain the psychological safety of the class.
🐼 He Gentle and considerate little He
🎬 Action:When you see Jia raise the relay flag, take a deep breath, straighten your chest, and smoothly continue reciting the next sentence.
"Thank you, Jia, for helping me relay!"Now I take a deep breath and read the next sentence!”
💡 Tips:Help He regain courage from peer relay and overcome reading inferiority complex.
🦊 Jia Enthusiastic and rule-abiding Jia
🎬 Action:Immediately raise the green relay flag and help read the four words that are stuck in a clear and loud voice.
"The breeze is blowing the willow trees!" He, I'll let you continue. You read it very nicely! ”
💡 Tips:Guiding Jia is keenly aware of the difficulties of peers and exerts team spirit to proactively fill in the gaps and provide support.

⏳Tick-tock clock adagio pranayama
🏷️ Inspiration Library Topic 3: Classroom Learning Frustrations and Homework Challenges 📌 Field:📝 Classroom learning
🎖️ Today’s Badge: Calm Timing Expert

⏱️ The timer in class is ticking and I am so nervous - Facing time pressure, "take a deep breath according to the rhythm and take a breath for each question"

🎯 Summary of core objectives:The shrinking red block or ticking sound of the countdown timer on the large screen often causes autistic and learning-disabled children to experience extreme anxiety, sweaty palms, and a complete mental blank. Teaching children to shift their visual focus to their breathing circle and learn the rhythm of "taking a breath after finishing a problem" is helpful.

📖 Classroom situation adventure story island and questions Arouse empathy · Aware of challenges
💣 A red countdown bomb and a leisurely little sea turtle!

Today in math class, we had a ten-minute pop quiz with five questions. A huge red countdown timer was projected in the center of the electronic whiteboard. Tick-tock, tick-tock, tick-tock… As the red time disc shrank, the hands emitted a rapid electronic beep. Sitting in the second row, Yu stared at the red circle, his heart pounding as if it would jump out of his throat! His palms were sweating profusely as he gripped his pencil. The addition and subtraction he usually knew were now a tangled mess in his head! Yu frantically crumpled his test paper into a ball: “It’s going to explode! I can’t finish!” The teacher walked to the large screen, pressed the “mute mode” on the timer, and placed a slowly flowing “blue turtle liquid hourglass” on Yu’s desk: “Yu, time isn’t a bomb chasing you, but a good friend accompanying you. Watch the turtle slowly swim, take a deep breath after finishing each question, and let’s move forward at our own pace!” Yu watched the turtle slowly descend, exhaled a long breath, his brain rebooted, and he smoothly finished the questions, stroke by stroke!

🤔 Class discussion guidance questions:When you see the clock counting down and you feel panicked, will crumpling up the exam paper buy you time? How can you calm your mind and write slowly?
🎭 Four character situation mini theater 🦁Yu 🐻Jun 🐼He 🦊Jia full-staff drill
🎬 Today's drill scenario:The timed quiz is in progress, and the four little heroes are practicing overcoming the pressure of time and maintaining steady breathing to answer the questions!
🦁 Yu Calm and self-disciplined Yu
🎬 Action:Look at the blue turtle hourglass on the table, take a deep breath and relax your shoulders, then write down the equations one by one in sequence.
"Time is not a bomb. Turtles swim slowly. I will calculate each question one by one. I can figure it out!"”
💡 Tips:Guide Yu to replace the anxious countdown stimulus by stabilizing the visual flow rate.
🐻 Jun A courageous and responsible young man
🎬 Action:After finishing the third question, I felt a little anxious, so I put my hands on the table and took a deep breath. I didn't guess the answer randomly before handing in the paper.
"Huh~ I won't make random guesses!" There are still five minutes left. I have to carefully check and calculate the remaining two questions! ”
💡 Tips:Guide students to overcome the impulsive rush mentality and cultivate patience in checking and calculating.
🐼 He Gentle and considerate little He
🎬 Action:Use a ruler to read the problem line by line slowly. Although the speed is slow, each step is calculated very thoroughly.
"Although I write slowly, the teacher said that you are a true hero if you write what you know how to write correctly!"”
💡 Tips:Guidance and affirmation of self-learning pace, not affected by the speed of peers submitting papers.
🦊 Jia Enthusiastic and rule-abiding Jia
🎬 Action:Quietly help the whole class maintain a peaceful examination room, and write down the remaining minutes on the blackboard when appropriate.
"Everyone, relax, there is still plenty of time, take a deep breath, and write slowly!"”
💡 Tips:Guidingjia calms the anxiety of the audience through gentle reminders.

🍫 Segment the chocolate into sections
🏷️ Inspiration Library Topic 3: Classroom Learning Frustrations and Homework Challenges 📌 Field:📝 Classroom learning
🎖️ Today’s badge: Master of problem solving

📐 Long Word Problems: Breaking Information into Small Parts

🎯 Summary of core objectives:Faced with math literacy word problems that often consist of four or five lines of text, children with reading difficulties and autism often fail to grasp the key words and give up, overwhelmed by the dense text. Teaching them to use a two-color highlighter to solve the problem like "cutting three chocolates" involves breaking down the condition, the number, and the question.

📖 Classroom situation adventure story island and questions Arouse empathy · Aware of challenges
🍫 A giant chocolate block with three magical little cutters!

The last problem on the math workbook was a real nightmare, stretching for four long lines: "There are three classes in the fourth grade of OO Elementary School, with twenty-five students in each class. Each bus ticket for a field trip costs 100 yuan. How much will all the students have to pay for the tickets in total?" He felt his scalp tingle when he saw those four long lines of densely packed black text. His eyes kept skipping lines, completely confused about whether to add or multiply. He grabbed his hair and sighed, "It's too long! I can't even understand it! Why write math problems like they're from a storybook!" The teacher smiled and took out a thick bar of chocolate, handing He pink and yellow highlighters: "He, swallowing a big piece of chocolate whole will choke you. Let's cut it into three pieces! First cut: find out 'who is doing what'; second cut: circle the 'numbers and units'; third cut: use yellow to highlight 'what the question is actually asking!'" He cut the problem three times, and what was originally a long, monstrous problem instantly became a neat three-step equation. He excitedly shouted, "It's so simple once you cut it! I can do it!"

🤔 Class discussion guidance questions:When you see a long and difficult question, what happens if you try to guess the answer without even looking at it? Why does using a highlighter to cut through the question make it clearer to the brain?
🎭 Four character situation mini theater 🦁Yu 🐻Jun 🐼He 🦊Jia full-staff drill
🎬 Today's drill scenario:Faced with a complex and lengthy math word problem, the four little heroes practice using highlighters to break down the core information into segments!
🦁 Yu Calm and self-disciplined Yu
🎬 Action:Use the transparent green reading ruler to cover the irrelevant text below and focus on analyzing the conditional information in the first line.
"Looking slowly, row by row, the first piece of chocolate is from three classes, with twenty-five people in each class!"”
💡 Tips:Guide Yu to reduce global information overload interference through visual focusing tools.
🐻 Jun A courageous and responsible young man
🎬 Action:Use a pencil to circle the three key numbers 3, 25, and 100 quickly and write out the multiplication equation.
"Circle the numbers so they won't get messed up!" 25 times 3 equals 75, multiply that by 100 and you’re done! ”
💡 Tips:Guide the team to combine agile thinking with step marking to improve computing efficiency.
🐼 He Gentle and considerate little He
🎬 Action:Use the yellow highlighter to draw the last sentence, and show a bright and confident smile.
"The question asks how much the total ticket cost!" Cut into three pieces of chocolate, and the long questions are no longer scary at all! ”
💡 Tips:Help He experience the reading comprehension breakthrough brought by visual deconstruction.
🦊 Jia Enthusiastic and rule-abiding Jia
🎬 Action:Draw a diagram of the three tour buses on the whiteboard to help the whole group visually verify the results.
"Draw three pictures of tourist buses, and everyone can see at a glance whether the calculations are correct!”
💡 Tips:Guidance and graphical representation are combined to strengthen the logical thinking structure.

Provide a visual mask (reading window), which only exposes one line of text at a time to prevent the line of sight from being disturbed by the full-page long text.
🔹 Students with Learning Disabilities (LD)
Use a two-color fluorescent pen: draw the condition information in pink, draw the core question sentence in yellow, and circle the numbers with a ball pen.

Before you encounter a long question and feel like throwing down the textbook, do the "cutting chocolate three times" action to relax your mind.

🪐 Unique Planetary Pride
🏷️ Inspiration Library Topic 3: Classroom Learning Frustrations and Homework Challenges 📌 Field:📝 Classroom learning
🎖️ Today’s badge: Creative and confident little painter

🎨 Art Is Unique: Letting Go of Perfection

🎯 Summary of core objectives:Children with autism are often bound by a strong sense of perfectionism and fixation on symmetry. If they paint outside the black lines in their watercolor paintings or their clay sculptures are slightly different from the teacher's model, they may break down in tears, crushing and stomping on their artwork. It is important to guide children to accept that "difference is precisely what makes art unique."

📖 Classroom situation adventure story island and questions Arouse empathy · Aware of challenges
🌌 A crooked flying saucer and a colorful rainbow star!

Today's art class theme was to sculpt a "magical space station" using lightweight clay. The teacher displayed a neat, symmetrical, silver-white rocket template on the platform. Yu tried to copy it, but because the clay was too soft, the rocket's tip was slightly tilted to the left by three centimeters, and he couldn't straighten it no matter how hard he tried. Looking at his crooked rocket, Yu's face turned bright red, his fists clenched and trembled. He grabbed the rocket, ready to smash it to the ground: "It's ruined! It doesn't look like the teacher's at all! I'm such an idiot!" The teacher gently reached out and caught Yu's clay: "Yu, wait! Look at the clouds outside the window. Are there any clouds that look exactly the same? If everyone's spaceship looked the same, how boring would the universe be! Your rocket's tip is bent to the left, just like a magical cruiser nimbly dodging an asteroid!" Yu was stunned. He looked at the curved rocket in his hand and suddenly thought it was so cool. Yu added two more small stars next to it and smiled happily: "This is my own 'Starship Scimitar'!"

🤔 Class discussion guidance questions:When your drawing or art piece is different from the template, will smashing or stepping on it make you feel better? Why is something different the most special treasure?
🎭 Four character situation mini theater 🦁Yu 🐻Jun 🐼He 🦊Jia full-staff drill
🎬 Today's drill scenario:The clay sculpture was accidentally sculpted crookedly. The four little heroes practiced breaking free from the constraints of perfectionism and appreciating unique creativity!
🦁 Yu Calm and self-disciplined Yu
🎬 Action:Looking at the crooked rocket, put down your hand that you want to smash, take a deep breath, tilt your head and add yellow clay to turn it into a thruster.
"It's not broken because it's crooked. My rocket is the most flexible interstellar cruiser in the universe!"”
💡 Tips:Guide Yu to break the symmetry fixation and reconstruct the unexpected results into unique creative highlights.
🐻 Jun A courageous and responsible young man
🎬 Action:If you accidentally paint outside the black line with watercolor, don't tear off the paper. Instead, use blue to paint a wave pattern.
"It doesn't matter if I paint the outside of the grid, I'll paint it into a big wave and turn it into a super waterfall!"”
💡 Tips:Guidance to transform small setbacks into flexible artistic sense of humor.
🐼 He Gentle and considerate little He
🎬 Action:Gently sculpt a round little snowman with your hands and happily show your creation to everyone.
"Although my snowman's belly is one big and one small, he is smiling and I think he is so cute!"”
💡 Tips:Help He experience the beautiful feeling of self-acceptance and build positive self-esteem.
🦊 Jia Enthusiastic and rule-abiding Jia
🎬 Action:Arrange the four different spaceships together in front of the podium to form a space fleet.
"It's fun if all four ships are different!" Together, we are the strongest space fleet in OO Elementary School! ”
💡 Tips:Guide and praise the beauty of heterogeneity and condense the collective sense of honor of diverse integration.

📁 Five-Color Storage Magic

🎒 An Organized School Bag: Color Folders and a Daily Check

🎯 Summary of core objectives:Children with ADHD and learning disabilities often have weak executive functions, resulting in their schoolbags being stuffed with crumpled notices, moldy breadcrumbs, and scattered colored pens. They experience anxiety when they can't find their homework during class and are punished. We teach them the "five-color folder sorting method" and a three-minute "detoxification and emptying check" before school ends.

📖 Classroom situation adventure story island and questions Arouse empathy · Aware of challenges
🕳️ A giant black hole backpack and a colorful rainbow folder!

When collecting Chinese homework during morning self-study, everyone in the class had handed it in, except for Jun, who was still rummaging through his big backpack! Jun's backpack was crammed full, like a giant black hole about to explode. Inside were last week's notices crumpled like dried plums, broken crayon stubs, half-eaten cookie bags, and three textbooks with their corners folded upside down. Jun was sweating profusely, almost going crazy: "Strange! I clearly wrote it yesterday, where did it go! So annoying!" Frustrated, Jun dumped all the clutter from his backpack onto the hallway floor. The teacher walked over and took out five transparent folders of different colors: "Jun, your backpack isn't a trash can, it's your learning toolbox! Let's do a 'five-color detox': blue for Chinese, red for math, yellow for the communication book, and green for the notices!" Under the teacher's guidance, Jun threw the clutter into the trash can, neatly categorized the five subjects, and the missing vocabulary book suddenly jumped out from the blue folder! Jun hugged his neatly packed schoolbag and smiled proudly!

🤔 Class discussion guidance questions:How anxious do you feel when you can't find your homework book during class? What are the benefits of tidying up your schoolbag after school each day for yourself tomorrow?
🎭 Four character situation mini theater 🦁Yu 🐻Jun 🐼He 🦊Jia full-staff drill

🦁 Yu Calm and self-disciplined Yu
🎬 Action:Following the order of blue Mandarin and red Math labels, neatly pull out the vocabulary book from your schoolbag and hand it to the group leader.
"The blue label is for Mandarin homework. I found it right away. The schoolbag is neat and comfortable!"”
💡 Tips:Guide Yu to give full play to the strengths of classification and establish a structured school bag order.
🐻 Jun A courageous and responsible young man
🎬 Action:Pick up the scraps of paper from your schoolbag and put them in the trash can. Then, neatly arrange the five-colored folders and put them back in your schoolbag.
"Phew~ My big black hole schoolbag has been detoxified!"Now it only takes three seconds to find something!”
💡 Tips:Guide the establishment of executive functions and the organization of personal life items management.
🐼 He Gentle and considerate little He
🎬 Action:Look at the backpack check card, check the pencil case and communication book one by one, zip up the bag and smile.
"Tick the cards and bring all the homework. You don't have to worry about being missed when you go home today!" ”
💡 Tips:Help He use checklists to overcome forgetfulness anxiety and enhance a sense of autonomy.
🦊 Jia Enthusiastic and rule-abiding Jia
🎬 Action:Show the neatly organized inner lining of your backpack in front of the podium and encourage everyone to keep it clean.
"It only takes three minutes to pack your schoolbag every day, and you won't be in a hurry to find it in class tomorrow!" ”
💡 Tips:Guide Jia to demonstrate good living routines and become a model of cleanliness in the class.
