🤝 No complaints when the team drops a baton
🏷️ Inspiration Library Topic 3: Classroom Learning Frustrations and Homework Challenges 📌 Field:📝 Classroom learning
🎖️ Today’s Badge: Best Teammate

🏃 A Dropped Relay Baton: Supporting a Teammate

🎯 Summary of core objectives:In relay races or team competitions, if a teammate slips the baton or runs the wrong lane, causing the entire group to fall behind, emotionally challenged children are prone to verbally abusing them, shouting things like, "It's all your fault! You're terrible!" This can lead to serious peer bullying. The correct approach is to "immediately go up to them, pat them on the back, and say, 'It's okay, let's catch up together.'"

📖 Classroom situation adventure story island and questions Arouse empathy · Aware of challenges
🥉 The golden baton rolled off the red track!

On the eve of the school sports meet, during PE class, a tense and exciting fourth-grade relay simulation was underway. Jun ran the fourth leg, sprinting like a whirlwind and successfully catching up to second place! At the baton exchange area, Jun shouted, "Pass the baton!" However, He, who was supposed to receive the fifth leg, was so nervous with sweaty palms that her outstretched hand slipped, and the golden baton slammed onto the red PU track with a loud "thud!" rolling all the way into the grass! The teams behind seized the opportunity to overtake, and the lead instantly turned into last place. Jun's eyes blazed with anger, and she clenched her fists, about to rush towards He and yell, "What are you doing! You're so stupid! You're the one who made us lose!" Seeing this, Jia immediately rushed over, picked up the baton, and shoved it back into He's hand, shouting, "He, don't stop! Keep going! Jun, yelling now will only slow things down, let's all cheer her on from the sidelines!" Jun paused for a moment, watching He grit his teeth and sprint forward. He swallowed the curse words he was about to utter, put his hands to his mouth and shouted, "Go He! Go for it!" The whole class cheered along, and He sprinted like he had a turbocharger, finally catching up with one person just before the finish line!

🤔 Class discussion guidance questions:When a teammate makes a mistake during a competition, will yelling at them on the spot bring back the ranking? Why is saying "It's okay, we'll catch up together" the coolest way to be a teammate?
🎭 Four character situation mini theater 🦁Yu 🐻Jun 🐼He 🦊Jia full-staff drill
🎬 Today's drill scenario:During a relay race, a teammate's nervousness caused them to drop the baton, resulting in them falling behind. The four little heroes practiced restraining their blaming and demonstrating team tolerance and drive!
🦁 Yu Calm and self-disciplined Yu
🎬 Action:Stand in front of the finish line and wave the cheering flag vigorously, cheering loudly for He who is sprinting after dropping the baton.
"He rushes!" Looking at the finish line ahead, everyone who finishes the race is a hero! ”
💡 Tips:Guide Yu to maintain positive emotional stability and give strength to his peers when he is at a disadvantage in the competition.
🐻 Jun A courageous and responsible young man
🎬 Action:Take a deep breath and swallow your accusations, then clap your hands and shout loudly to cheer for He.
"Huh ~ I don't curse!"Come on He! You run very fast, take big strides and rush over!”
💡 Tips:The leader sublimates the aggressive energy into the leadership spirit that unites the team's fighting spirit.
🐼 He Gentle and considerate little He
🎬 Action:Pick up the baton on the grass, grit your teeth, swing your arms and sprint towards the finish line, without giving up or stopping because of self-blame.
"Everyone didn't scold me and cheered for me. I must run every meter with all my strength!"”
💡 Tips:Help He gain motivation to resist setbacks from the tolerance of peers and persevere to the end.
🦊 Jia Enthusiastic and rule-abiding Jia
🎬 Action:Quickly guide the baton exchange route and remind everyone not to stand on the track and block the runners.
"Everyone, cheer on both sides of the runway, leave the road to He, we are the number one who will never give up!"”
💡 Tips:Guide Jia to maintain order on the field and implement safety and team organization.

📏 Accidentally damaged the Calm Ruler
🏷️ Inspiration Library Topic 4: Peer Friction and Conflict Resolution Advanced 📌 Field:🤝 Peer conflict
🎖️ Today’s Badge: Calm Mediation Judge

😡 Accident or Intent? Responding Calmly to Broken Things

🎯 Summary of core objectives:When a child with autism or emotional disorders accidentally steps on or breaks their beloved stationery, they often instinctively assume "it was intentional" and retaliate with a punch. Guiding children to "first observe their facial expressions, clarify the accident, and seek compensation and an apology from the teacher" can help prevent the violence from escalating.

📖 Classroom situation adventure story island and questions Arouse empathy · Aware of challenges
💔 A transparent dinosaur ruler broken in two and a sincere apology letter!

Today in math class, we had to draw straight lines. Yu took out his limited-edition "Glow-in-the-Dark Tyrannosaurus Rex Transparent Ruler," a new gift from his dad, and was extremely proud of himself. At the end of class, Jun rushed out of his seat to get a drink of water, but he stumbled and his elbow accidentally brushed against the ruler on Yu's desk. "Crack!" The precious Tyrannosaurus Rex ruler fell to the ground and was stomped in two by Jun! Looking at the broken ruler on the ground, Yu's blood pressure soared, his eyes turned bloodshot, and he roared like a wild beast. He grabbed Jun by the collar and raised his fist: "You deliberately broke my Tyrannosaurus Rex ruler! I'm going to kill you!" Jun turned pale with fright, his hands clasped in front of his chest as he shouted: "I didn't mean to! I really didn't see it! I'm sorry!" The teacher immediately stepped forward to separate the two: "Yu, stop! Take a deep breath! Do you see Jun grinning as he deliberately stepped on it, or is he trembling with fear?" "I can pay for broken items, but hitting someone will shatter a friend's heart!" Yu looked at the frightened Jun and slowly lowered his fist. Jun immediately ran back to his seat, took out a brand new iron ruler, and handed it to Yu: "Yu, I'm sorry. I'll tell my mom after school that I'll definitely buy you an identical one!" Yu took the iron ruler, and the anger in his heart finally subsided.

🤔 Class discussion guidance questions:When someone breaks your favorite toy or stationery, will punching them fix it? Distinguish between "accidental" and "intentional" damage, and why does it protect friendship?
🎭 Four character situation mini theater 🦁Yu 🐻Jun 🐼He 🦊Jia full-staff drill
🎬 Today's drill scenario:A classmate accidentally steps on and breaks a student's beloved stationery. The four little heroes practice restraining their punches, recognizing the accident, and rationally resolving the situation!
🦁 Yu Calm and self-disciplined Yu
🎬 Action:Take a deep breath while looking at the broken ruler, release your grip on your classmate's collar, and proactively report to the teacher.
"Huh~ My heart hurts, but I know you were careless. Let's ask the teacher to help discuss compensation!" ”
💡 Tips:Guangyu can still follow rational procedures to protect his rights when his extremely cherished items are damaged.
🐻 Jun A courageous and responsible young man
🎬 Action:Lower your hands to show sincerity, do not shirk responsibility or run away, and bow on the spot to admit your mistake.
"I'm sorry Yu!" I ran too fast and bumped into one. I promise to ask my mother to buy a brand new one for you after school!”
💡 Tips:Guide people to have the courage to bear subsequent liability for compensation when they get into trouble, and not to evade with excuses.
🐼 He Gentle and considerate little He
🎬 Action:Hold the transparent tape and squat down to carefully help put the ruler that was broken in two back together and put it into the bag.
"Don't cry, Yu. I'll help you fix it with tape first. You can still see the tyrannosaurus pattern clearly!" ”
💡 Tips:Help He soothe the client's frustration and anxiety with gentle restorative actions.
🦊 Jia Enthusiastic and rule-abiding Jia
🎬 Action:Take out the class life agreement notebook, record the incident fairly, and guide both parties to shake hands and make peace.
"No one wants the accident to happen. Jia sincerely apologizes and promises compensation. Yu forgives. We are still good friends!" ”
💡 Tips:Guide Jia to use fair mediation procedures to maintain the rule of law and peace in the class.

👥 Sharing Friends: Making Room for Other Friendships

🎯 Summary of core objectives:Children with autism often have a strong sense of possessiveness and ownership in their friendships. If a close friend talks to other classmates or joins a group, they may feel betrayed, become angry, and break off the friendship or threaten to do so. We should teach them that "everyone can have many friends, and sharing with friends is more fun."

📖 Classroom situation adventure story island and questions Arouse empathy · Aware of challenges
🎈 A giant balloon with two ropes and a three-person jump rope team!

In the special education classroom, He always considered Jia her "most exclusive best friend." Every day after class, they would sit together under the shade of a tree and draw. Today, during the long break, Jia excitedly ran off with a jump rope to play "three-person jump rope" with two girls from the regular class. Everyone laughed happily in the hallway. Sitting by the window, He watched this scene, her heart aching with jealousy. He angrily bit her pencil, her eyes reddening, and secretly vowed: "Jia betrayed me! She went to play with someone else, I'll never talk to Jia again!" The teacher walked over to He, smiling as she took out a string of colorful balloons: "He, do you think balloons look better held in one hand, or floating in the sky so everyone can see them? Friends aren't dolls; we can't lock them away in our own closets. Jia going to jump rope doesn't mean she doesn't like you anymore; if you went over and loudly asked, 'Can I help you swing the rope?' wouldn't you all become best friends?" He wiped away her tears and went outside, shouting, "Jia, I'll help you swing the rope!" The four of them held hands and jumped in the sunlight, their laughter louder than ever before!

🤔 Class discussion guidance questions:When your favorite friend goes to play with someone else, can getting angry and severing ties bring them back? Why is it that accepting that a friend has other friends helps the friendship last?
🎭 Four character situation mini theater 🦁Yu 🐻Jun 🐼He 🦊Jia full-staff drill
🎬 Today's drill scenario:Seeing their best friend having fun with other classmates, the four little heroes practice letting go of their possessiveness and actively integrating into the group!
🦁 Yu Calm and self-disciplined Yu
🎬 Action:Seeing that Jun, whom she usually reads dinosaur books with, was playing dodgeball with others, she went to the library to read books, looking relaxed.
"Jia is very happy to play ball, and I can also enjoy dinosaur time in the library. We are still good friends after school! ”
💡 Tips:Guide Yu to establish healthy social differentiation and ability to handle herself independently.
🐻 Jun A courageous and responsible young man
🎬 Action:Seeing He standing to the side watching, the child runs over and waves, inviting him: "He, come play with me!"
"Come on He!" We are short of a super captain who can rock the rope. You are the best and most stable! ”
💡 Tips:The guidance department will pay keen attention to the single peers and actively build bridges for integration.
🐼 He Gentle and considerate little He
🎬 Action:Put aside your jealousy and anxiety, walk forward confidently, pick up the jump rope handle, and laugh with everyone.
"Let me help you shake the rope!" Seeing everyone jumping so high makes me feel so happy!”
💡 Tips:Help He break the narrow sense of interpersonal exclusivity and experience the joy of group acceptance.
🦊 Jia Enthusiastic and rule-abiding Jia
🎬 Action:After jumping rope, the first person to run over and give He a tight hug to thank him for his hard work swinging the rope.
"Thank you, He!" Only if you help us shake the rope can we jump to a new record of thirty times! ”
💡 Tips:Guide Jia to give exclusive emotional guarantee and affirmation to peers in a timely manner.

1
I sensed a pang of possessive jealousy, a feeling of wanting to get angry and break off the friendship.
2
Silently remind yourself: "Friends are not exclusive toys; they also have the freedom to make new friends."
3
Take the initiative to approach them and try to play together, or happily do your own thing.

🔹 Students with Learning Disabilities (LD)
Use children's songs to establish concepts: "One person plays alone, two people play warm, and everyone has fun!"
🔹 Students with Emotional Disorders (EBD)
Before jealousy breaks out and you want to break off the relationship, take three deep breaths and practice taking the initiative to join in or find other interesting things to do by yourself.

🗣️ Hurtful Nicknames: Speak Firmly and Ask a Teacher for Help

🎯 Summary of core objectives:Special needs students are often teased by their peers behind their backs for their unusual movements or stuttering, being called "freaks," "robots," or "fat boys." The goal is to teach these students to activate their "verbal defense" by giving them a firm look and saying, "That's not my name, please call me by my real name!" and to proactively report such remarks to their teachers.

📖 Classroom situation adventure story island and questions Arouse empathy · Aware of challenges
🦔 Spiky, offensive labels and glittering name badges!

Walking down the corridor, Jun heard two older students laughing and joking behind him: "Look, that robot who walks like a penguin is here again! Robot! Beep beep beep!" Jun, walking ahead, heard this and knew they were laughing at his forceful arm swing while walking. The word "robot" pierced Jun's ears like a poisonous thorn! Jun instantly flew into a rage, turned around, grabbed the lid of a nearby trash can, and was about to smash it over the other student's head! Jia happened to be passing by and immediately grabbed Jun's arm, shouting: "Jun, stop! If you hit someone, you lose! They just want to see you lose your temper!" Jia stood in front of Jun, looking directly at the two mocking students, her voice loud and firm: "He has a name, his name is Jun from OO Elementary School! Giving someone such an offensive nickname is extremely rude! We're going to the student affairs office to report him to the teacher right now!" Seeing Jia's resolute courage, the two classmates turned red with fright, lowered their heads, and slunk away. Jun put down the bucket lid, took a deep breath, and said, "Jia, thank you. If I had acted just now, I would have received a major demerit!"

🤔 Class discussion guidance questions:When someone calls you a mean nickname, if you immediately become enraged and hit them, who will be punished? Why is responding with a firm and confident attitude and going to the teacher the smartest thing to do?
🎭 Four character situation mini theater 🦁Yu 🐻Jun 🐼He 🦊Jia full-staff drill
🎬 Today's drill scenario:The four little heroes are provoked by malicious and offensive nicknames in the corridor. They practice activating their verbal defense shield, firmly defending themselves, and seeking legitimate means!
🦁 Yu Calm and self-disciplined Yu
🎬 Action:When you hear malicious provocation, stand up straight, look the other person straight in the eye, and speak calmly and firmly.
"Please stop your behavior!"My name is Yu, don't call me any nickname!”
💡 Tips:Guide Yu to establish self-dignity with confident, unflinching body and spoken language.
🐻 Jun A courageous and responsible young man
🎬 Action:Put down the trash can lid you've grabbed, take a deep breath, and restrain the urge to retaliate with violence.
"Hoo~ I won't fall into your trap!" If you take action, you will only get a demerit. I will report to the instructor now! ”
💡 Tips:Guide people to see clearly the traps behind provocations and choose wise and legal channels for safeguarding their rights.
🐼 He Gentle and considerate little He
🎬 Action:Stand by Jun's side and hold his hand tightly, offering him unwavering support and companionship.
"Don't be afraid, Jia, we are all here to support you, let's go find the teacher together!"”
💡 Tips:Help He play the role of sympathetic supporter to avoid being left alone by the victimized peers.
🦊 Jia Enthusiastic and rule-abiding Jia
🎬 Action:Bravely step forward and look the provocateur in the eye, and firmly point out the errors and consequences of their remarks.
"Calling people ugly nicknames is bullying!"Please apologize to Jia immediately, otherwise we will report it to the Academic Affairs Office immediately!”
💡 Tips:Guide Jia to develop a sense of justice and use the legal and school rules to fight against bullies.

🤝 Group Decisions: Voting and Respecting Everyone

🎯 Summary of core objectives:When creating posters or discussing topics in groups, autistic children often become fixated on their own ideas, insisting that the entire group listen to their chosen theme, otherwise they will bang on the table, get up, and cry. We should teach them democratic compromise mechanisms such as "majority rule," "best-of-three," and "incorporating different elements."

📖 Classroom situation adventure story island and questions Arouse empathy · Aware of challenges
🦖 Green Dinosaur vs. 🚀 The decisive battle of Silver Rocket!

During group activity time in the special education classroom, the teacher asked four little heroes—Yu, He, Jia, and Jun—to work together to draw a large poster on the blackboard titled "Our Dreamland." At the start of the discussion, Yu slammed his fist on the table: "We have to draw 'Tyrannosaurus Rex Jurassic Park'! Only dinosaurs are the strongest! We have to draw all dinosaurs!" Jia immediately jumped up and retorted: "No! Dinosaurs every time! I want to draw 'Space Mars Base'! The silver rocket is the coolest!" The two argued back and forth, growing louder and louder. Yu, exasperated, slammed the eraser on the floor, crossed his arms, turned around, and shouted: "If we don't draw dinosaurs, I'm quitting! I won't draw any of them!" At this moment, Jun walked over and drew a line in the middle of the blackboard: "Stop! Everyone, don't argue! We have a democratic trick for different opinions—voting and unification! If three people vote for Space Base, the minority must obey the majority; but! We can draw a 'Tyrannosaurus Rex guarding the entrance to Space Base,' so that dinosaurs and rockets are in the same paradise!" Yu paused for a moment, imagining the Tyrannosaurus Rex wearing a space helmet, and couldn't help but burst out laughing: "Okay! A Tyrannosaurus Rex wearing a space helmet sounds really cool!" The four of them immediately picked up chalk and happily worked together to complete the best space dinosaur base in the whole school!

🤔 Class discussion guidance questions:During group discussions, if everyone insists on their own ideas and refuses to compromise, can the task be completed? Why can voting and combining everyone's ideas lead to a win-win situation?
🎭 Four character situation mini theater 🦁Yu 🐻Jun 🐼He 🦊Jia full-staff drill
🎬 Today's drill scenario:The group was stuck on the poster theme, so the four little heroes practiced using voting and creative ideas to reach a consensus as a whole!
🦁 Yu Calm and self-disciplined Yu
🎬 Action:Let go of your stubborn insistence and accept the compromise of changing your dinosaur into a space tyrannosaurus and integrating it into the rocket base.
"Okay!" It’s not all Jurassic, but the tyrannosaurus in the space hat is really cool, I agree! ”
💡 Tips:Guide Yu to demonstrate cognitive flexibility and compromise mind under the rules negotiation structure.
🐻 Jun A courageous and responsible young man
🎬 Action:Stand in front of the blackboard and act as the democratic moderator, proposing a creative solution that integrates the ideas of both sides.
"Arguing cannot solve the problem!" Everyone takes a step back. Dinosaurs wear spacesuits. The opinions of the whole group are taken into account!”
💡 Tips:Guidance turns leadership into team wisdom for coordinating conflicts and resolving deadlocks.
🐼 He Gentle and considerate little He
🎬 Action:Pick up a piece of chalk and draw a cute star next to the rocket to applaud the team's reconciliation.
"Everyone is no longer angry. It's happiest to paint together!" I painted a shiny helmet for the Tyrannosaurus! ”
💡 Tips:Help He actively engage in cooperative tasks to create a warm and positive team atmosphere.
🦊 Jia Enthusiastic and rule-abiding Jia
🎬 Action:Take the initiative to step forward and extend your hand to give Yu a high five, acknowledging Yu's magnanimity and cooperative spirit.
"Yu, thank you for your willingness to compromise!" After I finish drawing the space base, I will definitely listen to your ideas for the next theme! ”
💡 Tips:Guidance shows the democratic majority's gratitude to the compromiser and its commitment to future turns.

1
When you sense that everyone is at an impasse due to differing opinions, shout: "Let's vote!"
2
The side with fewer votes should maintain sportsmanship, smiling and cooperating with the majority decision
3

🔹 Students with Learning Disabilities (LD)
Use the physical "democratic voting chip" to put one into the carton. Whoever listens more will listen to the rules. The rules are clear and intuitive.
🔹 Students with Emotional Disorders (EBD)
When your opinion is rejected and you want to quit in anger, take three deep breaths and read the mantra aloud: "The minority obeys the majority, and it will be mine next time!"”

🖍️ The Dialogue Repair Technique with Colored Pencils
🏷️ Inspiration Library Topic 4: Peer Friction and Conflict Resolution Advanced 📌 Field:🤝 Peer conflict
🎖️ Today’s badge: A small model of gentle communication

💔 A Dried-Out Marker: Asking Kindly to Make Things Right

🎯 Summary of core objectives:When a kind person lends out colored pens, the cap may not be properly closed when the pens are returned, causing them to dry out and stop writing. Students often become upset and angry, yelling, "You did that on purpose! Pay me back! I'll never lend you a pen again!" Guiding students to use objective facts and gently request a pen loan or to work together to find an alternative solution is helpful.

📖 Classroom situation adventure story island and questions Arouse empathy · Aware of challenges
🍂 A dry, red colored pencil and a box of large, colorful puzzle pieces!

In art class, Jia kindly lent her 24-color pencils to Xiao Ming in the next group to draw a big red flower. Unexpectedly, when she returned them after class, her most frequently used "bright red" pencil had been left uncapped for the entire lesson, and the nib was as dry and hard as a twig, unable to draw any color on the paper! Seeing her beloved pencil broken, Jia felt a pang of heartache, almost bursting into tears. She wanted to rush over and smash Xiao Ming's pencil case on the ground, yelling, "You big bad guy! Give me a new pencil!" The teacher walked over to Jia, handing her a cup of warm water to soak the hardened nib: "Jia, it's normal to be angry, because you're upset that the pencil is broken. But yelling will only make Xiao Ming think you're insulting him. We can use the 'gentle repair dialogue method': point out the facts, express your distress, and offer concrete compensation!" Jia took a deep breath, went to Xiao Ming, and calmly said, "Xiao Ming, this pencil dried out because it wasn't capped, and I'm very sad that I can't draw now." "Could you lend me your red pen for this class, and return it to me next week with a new single red pen?" Xiaoming felt very guilty when he saw the dried-out pen and quickly handed his red pen to Jia with both hands: "Jia, I'm sorry! I was too careless. I will definitely ask my mother to buy you a new one when I get home today!" A storm of arguments that could have broken out instantly turned into a spring breeze.

🤔 Class discussion guidance questions:When something you lent to someone gets broken, will yelling at them or even physically smashing their things fix it? Why is it that asking for compensation in a calm and objective tone is more likely to elicit sincere reparations?
🎭 Four character situation mini theater 🦁Yu 🐻Jun 🐼He 🦊Jia full-staff drill
🎬 Today's drill scenario:The colored pencils lent to classmates dried out because the caps were not put back on. The four little heroes practiced calmly communicating and expressing their need for repair!
🦁 Yu Calm and self-disciplined Yu
🎬 Action:Help by taking out a small measuring cup filled with warm water and soaking the dried pen tip to perform emergency stationery treatment.
"Don't panic, Jia, soak the pen tip in warm water, maybe the ink inside can be saved!" ”
💡 Tips:Guidance Yu uses objective tool operations to focus on problem repair and resolve tensions.

🏃 After Bumping into a Younger Child - Stop and Ask an Adult to Check for Injury

🎯 Summary of core objectives:Hyperactive and impulsive children often run quickly down the hallways after school, accidentally knocking down younger students at corners. These children often run away out of fear of punishment or accuse the other child of blocking their way. We should teach them the responsibility of immediately crouching down to help them up and accompanying them to the health center.

📖 Classroom situation adventure story island and questions Arouse empathy · Aware of challenges
🚀 An unstoppable jet plane and a small water bottle on the ground!

As soon as the bell rang, fourth-grader Jun dashed out of the classroom like a fully fueled jet fighter! His arms outstretched like wings, his strides were incredibly fast, and he yelled, "Whoosh—! Plane landing!" Just as he rounded the corner of the stairs, a first-grader carrying a colorful water bottle happened to walk out. Jun was going too fast to stop, and with a loud "Bang!" the two collided violently! The little boy was sent flying, landing on the floor, his water bottle flying a considerable distance, his knee scraped and bleeding, and he immediately burst into tears! Jun's heart pounded in his chest. His first instinct was to turn and run back to the classroom, pretending nothing had happened. Just then, the teacher called out from behind, "Jun! A true hero doesn't run away after causing trouble! Stop!" Jun slammed on the brakes, turned around, and saw the little boy crying on the ground, tears and snot streaming down his face. Jun gritted his teeth, ran back to the little boy, knelt down, and gently picked up his water bottle: "Little brother, I'm so sorry! Big brother was running too fast and bumped into you. Where does it hurt? I'll take you to the health center to get some medicine!" Jun carefully helped the little boy up and slowly walked towards the infirmary. Although Jun had been reminded by his teacher not to run in the corridor, the nurse praised him: "You took responsible care of your younger brother; you're a brave and responsible young man!"

🤔 Class discussion guidance questions:When you accidentally knock down a younger student while running, what serious consequences will it cause if you turn and run away? Why is it that "crouching down to check on them and helping them apply medicine" shows you're a responsible older brother?
🎭 Four character situation mini theater 🦁Yu 🐻Jun 🐼He 🦊Jia full-staff drill
🎬 Today's drill scenario:While running around a corner, the four little heroes accidentally bumped into a younger student. They practiced overcoming their instinct to run away, crouching down to check on him, and taking responsibility for his care!
🦁 Yu Calm and self-disciplined Yu
🎬 Action:If you witness a collision, immediately step forward and help pick up the water bottle and textbooks that have fallen to the ground.
"Don't cry, little brother, the lid of the kettle is not broken, I will hold it for you!" Jia is helping you! ”
💡 Tips:Guide Yu to exert objective and calm auxiliary support ability at the accident scene.
🐻 Jun A courageous and responsible young man
🎬 Action:Overcome your fear of running away, turn around and squat down next to your junior, gently pat your junior's back, and look at him with apology and care in your eyes.
"I'm sorry, little brother, it was the big brother who rushed too fast and bumped into you!" I'll take you to the health center to apply medicine. Don't be afraid if you walk slowly!”
💡 Tips:Guide students to break through the defensive psychology of making mistakes and demonstrate the responsibility of senior students.
🐼 He Gentle and considerate little He
🎬 Action:Immediately run into the next classroom to inform the teacher and guide the teacher to come and assist in the situation.
"Report to the teacher, a younger brother in the lower grade fell down around the corner, and Jia is accompanying him!"”
💡 Tips:Help He quickly activate the adult support system to ensure medical and treatment safety.
🦊 Jia Enthusiastic and rule-abiding Jia
🎬 Action:Stand at the corner, make a slow-down gesture with both hands to remind the students running behind you to slow down.
"A classmate fell down at the corner of the corridor!" Please all students behind you please walk slowly and keep to the right! ”
💡 Tips:Guide and maintain safe movement lines around the accident site to avoid secondary collisions.

⚖️ Fair Play: Ask a Neutral Person to Check the Rules

🎯 Summary of core objectives:Special education students exhibit a strong fixation on rules and a strong sense of justice when playing Monopoly, stacking cups, or card games. If they discover that a peer has taken an extra step or an extra card, they immediately assume "he's cheating" and slam their fist on the table to overturn the outcome. They are taught to "pause with their hands forming a 'T' shape with their chest, take out the instruction manual, and check it calmly."

📖 Classroom situation adventure story island and questions Arouse empathy · Aware of challenges
🎲 The dice rolled a little more than usual, just like the Monopoly instruction manual!

Twenty minutes after class, four students were playing the exciting "Monopoly World Adventure" board game in the special education classroom. When it was Xiaoming's turn to roll the dice, a five rolled, but when his car piece reached the fourth square, he slipped and jumped directly to the sixth square, buying the high-speed rail station! Sitting opposite him, Jia, with eyes as sharp as an eagle, slammed her hand on the table, stood up, and yelled, "Cheating! Caught! You deliberately moved an extra square! You big cheater! This round doesn't count!" Enraged, Jia reached out and overturned the entire Monopoly board, scattering banknotes and houses all over the floor. Xiaoming stood frozen in shock. The teacher walked over and gently patted Jia's head: "Jia, it's very righteous of you to notice the incorrect move count. But as a referee, you need to have class. Overturning the board only ruins the game." When you think there's a problem with the rules, our superpower is—"make a T with both hands in front of your chest," and shout, "Stop! Let's look at the instructions and recount the steps!" That way, everyone will admire your professionalism and fairness! Jia, looking at the banknotes scattered on the floor, embarrassedly squatted down to help pick them up: "Sorry, Xiao Ming, I shouldn't have flipped the table. Let's recount the dice; five should be here!" Everyone sat down again, and the game was filled with laughter once more!

🤔 Class discussion guidance questions:When playing a board game and you think someone has made a mistake or cheated, will flipping the whole table solve the problem? Why is it that making a pause gesture and calmly checking the rules is more respected?
🎭 Four character situation mini theater 🦁Yu 🐻Jun 🐼He 🦊Jia full-staff drill
🎬 Today's drill scenario:A dispute arose over the number of moves during a board game duel. The four little heroes practiced starting and pausing gestures, calmly checking the rules without flipping the table!
🦁 Yu Calm and self-disciplined Yu
🎬 Action:Point carefully to the Monopoly grid squares and objectively and fairly recalculate the points for everyone.
"Don't make any noise, everyone. The dice is five o'clock, one, two, three, four, five. The chess piece should stop here!"”
💡 Tips:Guide Yu to exert meticulous and accurate observation skills and provide objective data to resolve disputes.
🐻 Jun A courageous and responsible young man
🎬 Action:Help pick up the colored banknotes that have fallen on the ground one by one and arrange them neatly, and take the initiative to soothe the opposing emotions.
"It's okay, it's okay, I just looked at the wrong grid. Just go again. Let's continue playing!" ”
💡 Tips:The leader maintains a friendly and gentle approach to the game and maintains harmony with peers.
🐼 He Gentle and considerate little He
🎬 Action:Take out the Monopoly instruction manual, point to the second rule, and read it aloud to the whole group.
"The instructions are very clear, just slide your hand and return to the previous square!" ”
💡 Tips:Help He make good use of objective written rules as the basis for fair decisions.
🦊 Jia Enthusiastic and rule-abiding Jia
🎬 Action:Resist the urge to flip the table, make a large "T" sign with both hands in front of your chest to pause, and speak calmly and firmly.
"Pause than T!" I don't lift the table, I am the impartial judge, let's count again! ”
💡 Tips:Guide Jia to transform a strong sense of justice into a civilized and professional refereeing style.

1
If you notice a suspected violation or a miscount of steps, immediately make a "T" sign to pause.
2
He said calmly, "Everyone, please pause for a moment. Let's go over the rules with the instruction manual."
3

👩‍🏫 A Substitute Teacher: Keeping Routines and Being Helpful

🎯 Summary of core objectives:When the original teacher is absent and a substitute teacher enters the classroom, it often causes extreme anxiety and maladjustment among autistic students, or students with emotional disorders take the opportunity to cause trouble and disrupt order. Teaching students to "follow established classroom rules and proactively introduce the class schedule to the substitute teacher" demonstrates good manners.

📖 Classroom situation adventure story island and questions Arouse empathy · Aware of challenges
👓 New glasses on the podium and a little class tour guide!

This morning, during the first period of Chinese class, it wasn't the familiar teacher who walked into the classroom, but Ms. Zhang, who wore silver-rimmed glasses and spoke with a soft voice. Ms. Zhang wrote her name on the blackboard: "The teacher is away for training today, so I'll be filling in for you all day!" Upon seeing the change of teacher, Yu tensed up, clutching his schoolbag tightly and repeatedly muttering, "Not the teacher! Not the teacher! The timetable is broken!" A few mischievous students in the back even took the opportunity to eat candy and chase each other down the hallway. At this moment, Jia stood up and shouted, "Stand up, salute! Good morning, teacher!" Jia stepped forward and handed Ms. Zhang a "Special Education Class Schedule": "Hello, Ms. Zhang. Every day, we read a story and take three deep breaths in the first period. I'm Jia, the class monitor, and we welcome you!" Seeing Jia's composure, Yu took a deep breath and slowly put down his schoolbag. Ms. Zhang smiled and stamped the whole class's record: "You are the most sensible and well-behaved class I've ever seen!" ”

🤔 Class discussion guidance questions:What happens if we deliberately cause trouble and create a disturbance when our familiar teacher is absent or a substitute teacher comes to class? Why is someone a true hero for proactively telling the new teacher about the class's good rules?
🎭 Four character situation mini theater 🦁Yu 🐻Jun 🐼He 🦊Jia full-staff drill

🎬 Action:Feeling a little uneasy facing a new teacher? Take out your usual visual timetable for reference, sit down comfortably, and take out your textbook.
"Although the teachers are different, the process of the Chinese class is the same, and I can concentrate on following the class!"”
💡 Tips:Guide Yu to overcome overreliance on specific people with constancy in task structure.
🐻 Jun A courageous and responsible young man
🎬 Action:Resist the urge to eat snacks in front of the substitute teacher and sit up straight.
"I don't take the opportunity to be naughty!" The teacher is not here, so I have to show discipline to the new teacher! ”
💡 Tips:Guide people to turn their competitive spirit into a sense of self-discipline and honor, and establish internal control traits.
🐼 He Gentle and considerate little He
🎬 Action:Gently offer a cup of warm water to the substitute teacher with both hands to express the class's warm welcome.
"Teacher Zhang, please drink water. Thank you for coming to teach us today. Thank you for your hard work!" ”
💡 Tips:Help He develop the caring and warm qualities, and actively establish friendly teacher-student interactions.
🦊 Jia Enthusiastic and rule-abiding Jia
🎬 Action:Stand up and lead the class in saluting, hand over the procedure card and proactively explain the speaking rules to the substitute teacher.
"Stand up and salute!" Hello Teacher Zhang, our class has to raise our hands to be called upon before speaking. We are ready! ”
💡 Tips:Guide Jia to give full play to his positive leadership talents and assist substitute teachers in quickly mastering class routines.

💺 New Seats: Three Ways to Get to Know a Classmate

🎯 Summary of core objectives:Children with autism exhibit a strong fixation on spatial locations. When the class reshuffles seating each month, they often cry and kick their desks, refusing to move because they feel they are "leaving their familiar, cozy spot by the window" or "having a classmate they don't like sitting next to them." We teach children to use three icebreaker phrases to help them adapt to new environments.

📖 Classroom situation adventure story island and questions Arouse empathy · Aware of challenges
🗺️ The wind blowing the school desks and chairs and the new neighbor's colored pencils!

At the beginning of each month, it's time for the whole class at OO Elementary School to change seats. The teacher announced the results of the draw: Yu would be moving from his safest spot in the corner with a wall to the second row in the middle, and next to him would be Jun, who usually talks very loudly! Upon seeing his new seat, Yu's heart sank. He clung to the corner of his desk, tears welling in his eyes, and protested loudly, "I don't want to move! That's my desk! There are too many people in the middle, it's scary!" The teacher came over and gently patted Yu's shoulder: "Yu, moving is like a little adventure. Sitting in the middle, you can see the words on the blackboard more clearly, and Jun is strong enough to help you carry your lunchbox! We'll use three 'icebreaker phrases' to get to know our new neighbors!" Yu took a deep breath, moved his backpack, and sat down in the middle. Jun immediately smiled broadly and gave Yu a newly bought dinosaur sticker: "Good morning, Yu! From now on, we're deskmates and best buddies!" Looking at the dinosaur stickers on the table, Yu finally felt relieved. It turns out that changing seats can also help you make good friends!

🤔 Class discussion guidance questions:If someone keeps crying and making a scene in their old seat when we change seats, can we refuse to change? When you move to a new seat, what's the first thing you should say to your new deskmate to make friends?
🎭 Four character situation mini theater 🦁Yu 🐻Jun 🐼He 🦊Jia full-staff drill
🎬 Today's drill scenario:The whole class changed seats and drew new neighbors. The four little heroes practiced overcoming spatial fixation, moving around confidently, and taking the initiative to break the ice!
🦁 Yu Calm and self-disciplined Yu
🎬 Action:Although you may not be used to being in the center, take a deep breath, arrange your stationery neatly on the table, and greet your deskmate.
"Good morning Jia, we will sit together in the future, please give me your advice!" ”
💡 Tips:Guide Yu to break the spatial fixation and take the first step to adapt to the new social circle with active speaking.
🐻 Jun A courageous and responsible young man
🎬 Action:Enthusiastically help Yu, who sits at the same table, move a chair, and take out stickers to share, showing friendliness and enthusiasm.
"Yu, welcome to the center!" I have a dinosaur sticker for you. Let’s finish the homework together! ”
💡 Tips:Guide students to accept new classmates with enthusiasm and tolerance, and eliminate the anxiety of special education peers.
🐼 He Gentle and considerate little He
🎬 Action:Wipe the new table clean and smile and nod to the new classmate next door.
"You can see the green trees outside the window from the new seat!" The view from this location is really nice! ”
💡 Tips:Help He explore the positive advantages of the new environment and cultivate an optimistic and adaptive mentality.
🦊 Jia Enthusiastic and rule-abiding Jia
🎬 Action:Help direct everyone to move the tables and chairs, and remind them to leave an arm's width of space near the aisle.
"Everyone's tables are arranged neatly, the chairs are put in, and the corridors are kept clear and safe!"”
💡 Tips:Guidance Jia plays an organizational maintenance function when the collective environment changes.

🚌 Tour bus etiquette guidelines
🏷️ Inspiration Library Topic 5: Special Situations and Environmental Adaptation 📌 Field:🏫 Environmental adaptation
🎖️ Today’s badge: Elegant little gentleman riding a car

🚌 Field-Trip Bus Safety: Stay Seated and Ask for Help

🎯 Summary of core objectives:When the whole school travels on large tour buses for field trips, special education students often become overly excited, chasing and jumping in the aisles, grabbing microphones and shouting, or breaking down in tears due to vestibular motion sickness and vomiting. They are taught to "fasten their seatbelts, quietly look out the window at the scenery, and immediately raise their hands to grab a vomit bag if they feel nauseous."

📖 Classroom situation adventure story island and questions Arouse empathy · Aware of challenges
⛰️ A wobbly bus and refreshing mint green candy!

Today is the annual autumn field trip, and the whole school is going on a two-hour bus tour to the Natural Science Museum! As soon as we got on the bus, Jun was extremely excited. He unbuckled his seatbelt and jumped around in the narrow aisle, shouting, "Go! Let's see who gets to the last row of big sofas first!" As the bus started moving and turned, Jun lost his balance and fell to the ground, almost hitting his forehead on the metal railing. The teacher came over and helped Jun up, saying seriously, "Running and jumping in the aisle while the bus is moving is very dangerous. If the driver brakes suddenly, you'll be thrown out like a missile!" The teacher helped Jun fasten his two-point seatbelt. At this moment, He, sitting by the window, turned pale from the swaying of the bus and clutched his stomach, feeling nauseous. Jia saw this and immediately took a plastic vomit bag from the storage pocket in front of his seat, raising his hand and shouting, "Teacher, He is feeling carsick and nauseous!" The teacher quickly handed out some mint candies and turned the air conditioner vent towards He's forehead. He sucked on the candy, looked out at the peaceful mountains, and his stomach gradually stopped churning. Everyone arrived safely and happily at the Science Museum!

🤔 Class discussion guidance questions:What terrible dangers might occur if you unbuckle your seatbelt and run around on a moving tour bus? What should you do if you feel dizzy and nauseous while riding in a vehicle?
🎭 Four character situation mini theater 🦁Yu 🐻Jun 🐼He 🦊Jia full-staff drill
🎬 Today's drill scenario:The school field trip begins, and the four little heroes practice fastening their seatbelts, maintaining good manners while riding, and looking after each other!
🦁 Yu Calm and self-disciplined Yu
🎬 Action:Once you get in the car, fasten your seatbelt, put on your earmuffs, and quietly watch the road scenery outside the window without making any noise.
"The seat belt is buckled!"Wearing earmuffs and looking at the big trees outside is like watching a movie. It’s so fun! ”
💡 Tips:Guide Yu to use sensory protection independently to regulate his mood in a remote closed vehicle.
🐻 Jun A courageous and responsible young man
🎬 Action:Resist the urge to run in the aisle, sit up straight, fasten your seatbelt, and quietly drink water from your water bottle.
"Huh~ Safety first!" I fastened my seat belt and sat down like a handsome little passenger who obeyed traffic regulations! ”
💡 Tips:Guidance is given to converge excess energy within the standardized framework to ensure one's own safety in riding a car.
🐼 He Gentle and considerate little He
🎬 Action:If you feel dizzy and nauseous, immediately raise your hand to express it, take a deep breath, suck on a mint, and look at the distant mountains.
"Looking at the green mountains in the distance, taking a deep breath, holding the cool candy in my mouth, my stomach feels much better!"”
💡 Tips:Help He timely detect physiological motion sickness warning signs and implement self-care.
🦊 Jia Enthusiastic and rule-abiding Jia
🎬 Action:Help check if your group members' seat belts are fastened, and promptly fetch cleaning bags for those who are motion sick.
"He, take this clean plastic bag, lean your head on the back of the chair and close your eyes. I'll be with you next to you!" ”
💡 Tips:Guide Jia to show the spirit of a general who helps each other and cares for each other during group travel.

1
Once you get in the car, immediately fasten your seatbelt around your waist and do not unfasten it unnecessarily.
2
Speak at a moderate volume, do not scream or run in the aisle
3
If you feel nauseous or dizzy, immediately grab a vomit bag and take a deep breath.

After returning home from school, show your parents how to🚌 Code of Civility on Tour Buses" and give a warm high-five to your family!

Use the picture card to demonstrate the "Three Don'ts of Riding in a Car": don't leave your seat, don't scream, and don't stick your head and hands out of the window.

Guide to transform excess excitement into a static mini-game of observing the scenery outside the window and playing "Counting Red Cars on the Road".

Food Preferences Sensory Needs and Asking for Support

Explain my food and sensory needs

A food smell makes Jia uncomfortable. Jia puts the utensils down safely and asks the teacher for help. Together they check the agreed dietary arrangements. The lesson practises expressing needs. Tasting food is not forced, and tolerating discomfort is not a condition for a reward.

🎲 Rainy Day Fun Box
🏷️ Inspiration Library Topic 5: Special Situations and Environmental Adaptation 📌 Field:🏫 Environmental adaptation
🎖️ Today’s badge: A little expert on how to deal with rainy days

🌧️ Heavy Rain: Choosing a Quiet Indoor Activity

🎯 Summary of core objectives:When it rains, the playground becomes muddy and closed. Special education students who are used to running and playing ball on the playground often become restless in the classroom, frantically sliding on bases in the corridor, or banging on doors and making noise. We guide the students to activate the "Rainy Day Indoor Fun Box" and learn to look at picture books, do puzzles, and play two-player static board games to calm their minds and bodies.

📖 Classroom situation adventure story island and questions Arouse empathy · Aware of challenges
🌧️ The big raindrops outside the window and the 3D Rubik's Cube on the table!

At 2 PM, a torrential downpour began, turning the playground into a vast expanse of water. The student affairs office announced over the loudspeaker: "Attention all students, the playground will be completely closed this afternoon. Please do not go outdoors after class!" Jun, who usually rushed to the playground to play basketball after every break, was like a caged cheetah, pacing restlessly in the corridor, stamping his feet: "What am I supposed to do if I can't play basketball! So boring! So incredibly boring!" He grabbed a basketball and began dribbling it wildly in the corridor, the deafening "thump! thump! thump!" The noise drew the attention of a teacher from the next class, who came out to protest. The teacher gently took the basketball away and pulled a gleaming "Rainy Day Indoor Treasure Box" from a cabinet: "Jun, it's raining heavily outside, the perfect time for a brain upgrade! Inside the box are a 3D maze ball, a 100-piece puzzle, and a two-player Connect Four game. Want to play a 'Connect Four Showdown' with me?" Jun looked at the exquisite four-in-a-row chessboard and sat down curiously. For fifteen minutes, Jun was completely focused on the chessboard, thinking about the layout, while listening to the pattering rain outside the window. He felt extremely calm: "Playing chess in the classroom on a rainy day is even more intellectually challenging and fun than playing ball!"

🤔 Class discussion guidance questions:What dangers and noise would it cause to dribble a basketball wildly in the hallway when it's raining heavily and we can't go to the playground? What static games can we play in the classroom to make our brains smarter?
🎭 Four character situation mini theater 🦁Yu 🐻Jun 🐼He 🦊Jia full-staff drill
🎬 Today's drill scenario:Heavy rain closes the outdoor playground. Four little heroes practice activating rain contingency plans and focus on indoor board games and reading!
🦁 Yu Calm and self-disciplined Yu
🎬 Action:I walked to the book corner, picked out a thick encyclopedia of the universe, and sat on a comfortable cushion to read it attentively.
"Listening to the sound of rain outside and looking at the map of the universe and galaxies, the classroom is so quiet, I feel very relaxed! ”
💡 Tips:Guide Yu to enjoy high-quality static reading time.
🐻 Jun A courageous and responsible young man
🎬 Action:Put the basketball into the bag and put it away. Sit at the table and play a game of Connect Four with your friends. Do not run around in the hallway dribbling the ball.
"Phew~ I won't shoot the ball!" Look at my line defense, playing chess requires more brainpower than playing basketball! ”
💡 Tips:The guide transfers the strong competitive spirit to the static chess and puzzle showdown.
🐼 He Gentle and considerate little He
🎬 Action:Take out a box of colored pencils and carefully fill in the color of the mandala drawing paper on a rainy day, stroke by stroke.
"After painting this colorful flower, my mood is as beautiful as seeing a rainbow after the rain!"”
💡 Tips:Help He use artistic creation to soothe emotions and improve concentration and persistence.
🦊 Jia Enthusiastic and rule-abiding Jia
🎬 Action:Help everyone distribute chessboards and pieces in the board game area, and remind everyone to put them back in their original place after playing.
"Everyone picks a board game on a rainy day. Remember to put the chess pieces back into the box after playing!"”
💡 Tips:Guide and maintain the order of indoor activity areas and the storage of teaching aids.

🗣️ Guiding words:"Kids watch the big screen!"Today the protagonist encounters a big test... If it were you, how would you feel?”

🎯 Super power move visual chart card ⭐ Three ways to stay indoors on a rainy day
1
Accept the fact that it's raining, take a deep breath and tell yourself: "Rainy days are peaceful and beautiful days."
2
Go to the classroom book corner or board game cabinet, choose a static item you like
3
Sit quietly and immerse yourself in the moment for thirty minutes, enjoying the peaceful time in the rain.
🎯 IEP Quantitative Goals & Putt Collaboration & Family Life Behavioral classification tripartite connection
🎯 IEP observable quantitative goals:When outdoor activities are limited on rainy days, students can independently choose and participate in static activities in the classroom (reading, educational board games, and painting) for more than 20 minutes without playing ball or collision in the corridor. The achievement rate is more than 85%.
🏫 Post-it notes on integration tips for regular class instructors:
Schools should open the library and indoor building block corner after class on rainy days, and assign senior service teams to patrol the corridors to maintain slow walking order.
🏠 Home Practice Check-In:
After returning home from school, show your parents how to🎲 "Record Fun Box for Rainy Days" and give warm high fives to your family!
🧩 Individualized differentiated support (support scaffolding for students with special needs) UDL multiple representation and participation
🔹 Students with autism spectrum disorder (ASD)
Design a "rainy day indoor activity list chart" and post it on the bulletin board: 1. Read the dinosaur encyclopedia 2. Puzzle challenge 3. Coloring mandala 4. Play chess duel.
🔹 Students with Learning Disabilities (LD)
Prepare board games with simple and intuitive rules (such as Kuaishou cup stacking, Tower of Babel building blocks, and four-piece chess) to lower the threshold of written rules.
🔹 Students with Emotional Disorders (EBD)
Before complaining about "being bored and wanting to throw the ball", take three deep breaths and be guided by the teacher into a one-to-one focused board game situation.

🎖️ Today’s badge: Clean and environmentally friendly little guard

🧹 Cleaning Tasks - Use Tools within an Agreed Safe Role and Avoid Splashing Others

🎯 Summary of core objectives:At the end of each semester, during the school-wide cleaning, special education students often run away or slack off due to tactile aversion to the blackened washbasins, moss-covered ditches, and dirty buckets, or get overly excited and splash water everywhere with hoses, soaking their classmates. The school teaches students to "divide tasks for washing, use water safely, and remember that labor is honorable."

📖 Classroom situation adventure story island and questions Arouse empathy · Aware of challenges
🧼 A sparkling handwashing station and a cleaning agent in rain boots!

This afternoon was OO Elementary School's once-a-semester "year-end cleaning"! The special education class was responsible for cleaning the central handwashing station and leaf-collecting ditch of the entire special education building. The ditch was filled with black, sticky, withered leaves, and green moss had grown in the grout lines of the handwashing station tiles. Upon seeing the mud, He retreated far away, waving his little hands: "So dirty! So disgusting! I don't want to touch it!" Jun, who was responsible for holding the long hose, got too excited and grabbed the hose, turning the water jet to maximum. "Whoosh—!" he sprayed water everywhere in the corridor like a fire truck, almost soaking Yu's pants and shoes! The teacher came over and turned off the tap: "Everyone, stop! The cleaning is a magical 'renewal operation,' not a water fight! As long as everyone puts on rain boots and waterproof gloves, we are cleaning agents defeating the dirt monster!" The teacher assigned tasks: He was responsible for wearing gloves and using long tongs to pick up fallen leaves; Jun was responsible for vigorously scrubbing the grout lines of the tiles with a stiff-bristled brush; Yu was responsible for squeegeeing the dirty water off the floor; and Jia was responsible for checking every corner. The four of them worked together for half an hour, and the originally blackened sink tiles became sparkling clean, like a mirror! Looking at the spotless sink, everyone felt a tremendous sense of accomplishment!

🤔 Class discussion guidance questions:If everyone is diligently scrubbing during a big clean-up, but you're just spraying water everywhere with a hose, what dangers might that pose? How would you feel if you personally cleaned a dirty and messy environment until it was sparkling clean?
🎭 Four character situation mini theater 🦁Yu 🐻Jun 🐼He 🦊Jia full-staff drill
🎬 Today's drill scenario:The whole school is cleaning and washing the handwashing stations and public areas. Four little heroes practice dividing tasks and cooperating, using water safely and not playing around!
🦁 Yu Calm and self-disciplined Yu
🎬 Action:Hold the long-handled squeegee firmly with both hands and push the water in the corridor smoothly towards the drain hole step by step, so that the floor dries quickly.
"Scrape all the water into the drainage holes, and the floor will be dry, so you won't slip when you walk!" ”
💡 Tips:Guide Yu to gain a high degree of concentration and control in regular and repetitive tool operations.
🐻 Jun A courageous and responsible young man
🎬 Action:Wear an apron and squat by the ditch. Use your hands to scrub the moss back and forth with a steel brush, and restrain the urge to play in the water.
"Hoo~ look at my powerful Vajra brush!" Brush all the black moss away and the sink becomes super white! ”
💡 Tips:Guidance is given to convert excess physical energy into a positive force for high-intensity cleaning work.
🐼 He Gentle and considerate little He
🎬 Action:Wearing thick gloves and holding long stainless steel tongs, carefully tuck each fallen leaf blocking the ditch into the dustpan.
"Wear gloves and you won't have to worry about dirty hands!" Clamp the fallen leaves cleanly and the water will flow smoothly! ”
💡 Tips:Help He eliminate tactile fear through protective assistive devices and actively participate in public services.
🦊 Jia Enthusiastic and rule-abiding Jia
🎬 Action:Be responsible for mixing the environmentally friendly cleaning agent on the side and pour an appropriate amount onto the tiles to ensure safe use.
"Pour three drops of eco-friendly orange water, it is fragrant and removes stains, and it saves effort for everyone to brush!"”
💡 Tips:Guide Jia to take on the detailed responsibilities of cleaning materials management.

1
Wearing a waterproof apron and rubber gloves will protect you from getting dirty.
2
Hold the long-handled brush firmly with both hands and scrub the dirt vigorously, keeping the hose pointing downwards to avoid spraying haphazardly
3
Scrape away the puddles, arrange the utensils neatly, and enjoy the sense of accomplishment from a cleaner environment.

🔹 Students with Learning Disabilities (LD)
Break down general cleaning into "clipping fallen leaves" ➡️ Pour detergent ➡️ Brush brush brush ➡️ "Scrape clean" four-frame clear process card.
🔹 Students with Emotional Disorders (EBD)
It is strictly prohibited to use clean water pipes as toys to shoot at each other. It is stipulated that the water outlet of the water pipe must always be close to the ground within thirty centimeters.

🛑 Strangers' Red Line Brakes
🏷️ Inspiration Library Topic 5: Special Situations and Environmental Adaptation 📌 Field:🏫 Environmental adaptation
🎖️ Today’s badge: Self-protection little guard

🚶 Stranger Safety: Do Not Go Along or Get into a Car

🎯 Summary of core objectives:Special education children are often naive and lack vigilance towards strangers, or are easily attracted by candy, Pokémon cards, or cute puppies. When a stranger in a car asks for directions and says, "Little one, get in the car and I'll buy you a drink," they readily get in. They should be taught the safety red lines: "Take three steps back, loudly refuse, and run to a convenience store for help."

📖 Classroom situation adventure story island and questions Arouse empathy · Aware of challenges
🚗 A black sedan with its windows rolled down and a gleaming convenience store door!

Walking home from school on the walkway, a black sedan suddenly pulled up to a stop, its window slowly rolling down. Inside sat a smiling stranger wearing sunglasses, holding a bag of sparkly limited-edition Pokémon card packs and a cute cat plush toy: "Hello, little friend! Uncle is lost at OO Elementary School. Could you sit in the front seat and help Uncle get directions? This whole set of Charizard card packs and this adorable cat plush toy is a thank you gift!" Jun's eyes lit up at the sight of the rare Pokémon cards, and he couldn't resist walking towards the car door, reaching out to take the pack! Yu, walking beside him, saw this and immediately panicked! Remembering the "stranger red line braking" drill they'd practiced in class, Yu rushed forward, grabbing Jun's backpack strap and shouting, "Jun, stop! You absolutely cannot get in the car!" Yu pulled Jun back three steps, shouting into the car window, "We don't know!" "We need to find a police officer!" With that, Yu and Jun grabbed their backpacks and rushed into the brightly lit FamilyMart convenience store at the intersection without looking back, shouting for help from the clerk: "Auntie! There are strangers outside asking us to get in their car!" The clerk immediately sheltered them behind the checkout counter and called the police. Seeing the situation was serious, the black car sped away! When the teacher and police arrived at the convenience store, they hugged the two children tightly and praised them: "Yu and Jun reacted so quickly! You successfully protected your lives!"

🤔 Class discussion guidance questions:When a stranger on the street offers you a fun toy or delicious snack and asks you to get in their car and show them the way, can you trust them? Why should you never get in their car no matter what they say?
🎭 Four character situation mini theater 🦁Yu 🐻Jun 🐼He 🦊Jia full-staff drill
🎬 Today's drill scenario:On their way home from school, four little heroes are approached by a stranger in a car who offers them gifts. They practice activating the safety red line, resisting the temptation, and running to the safety checkpoint!
🦁 Yu Calm and self-disciplined Yu
🎬 Action:When you see your peers about to be tempted, grab Jun's backpack strap, shout loudly, and lead the way to the convenience store for help.
"Xiaojiu, retreat quickly!" Never get into a stranger's car! We immediately ran to FamilyMart to find the clerk! ”
💡 Tips:Guide Yu to demonstrate precise vigilance and judgment and the courage to rescue his peers in highly crisis situations.
🐻 Jun A courageous and responsible young man
🎬 Action:Suddenly snapping back to reality, he pulled his hands back, turned around, and sprinted after Yu, not even glancing at the toy card holder behind him.
"Huh~ It's so dangerous that Yu can hold me!" No matter how rare a Pokémon card is, it is not as important as your own life! ”
💡 Tips:Guide people to overcome the temptation of greed and establish the understanding that personal safety is the absolute first priority.
🐼 He Gentle and considerate little He
🎬 Action:Walk together with others on the school trail, and immediately blow the high-frequency anti-wolf alarm whistle you carry if you see anything unusual.
"Beep——!" Blow the alarm whistle and let the adults around you look over, so the bad guys won't dare to approach! ”
💡 Tips:Help He make good use of self-defense alarm tools to make noise to scare off criminals.
🦊 Jia Enthusiastic and rule-abiding Jia
🎬 Action:Quickly note the color and characteristics of the suspicious vehicle, and clearly report it to the store clerk and police after entering the convenience store.
"Report to auntie, it's a black car with black film on the windows, and it ran away to the main road!"”
💡 Tips:Guide Jia to stay calm and observe in the panic and provide key clues to solve the case.

If a stranger tries to strike up a conversation while driving by, immediately take three steps back to maintain distance.

Shout loudly: 'I don't know, I need to find an adult!' Refuse to get into the car
3

🏫 Returning to the General Classroom: Finding My Group and Joining In

🎯 Summary of core objectives:Special education children, accustomed to the protection of small classes of one to four in disengagement special education classes, often feel lost and stand blankly at the door when the bell rings to return to a regular class of thirty students. This is because the classroom is noisy, they cannot find their seats, or they have missed the progress. We teach them the transition method of "looking at the blackboard homework before entering the classroom, smiling and nodding to the neighbor when walking to their seats".

📖 Classroom situation adventure story island and questions Arouse empathy · Aware of challenges
🚪 Two large doors and a green pass for traveling through time!

The school bell rang, signaling the end of class. Yu, having finished two lessons in the special education classroom, packed his bag and prepared to return to the large classroom of Class 2, Grade 4. Reaching the classroom door, Yu stopped, watching his thirty classmates laughing and playing loudly, the blackboard covered in densely packed Chinese Language Lesson 7 homework. A sudden, unfamiliar panic welled up inside Yu. He gripped his bag straps tightly, frozen like an outsider, hesitant to go in. Just then, the teacher slipped a "seamless transition card" into Yu's pocket: "Yu, the regular class is your stage! Do three things when you enter: First, look up at the blackboard to see what lesson it is; second, go to your seat and gently pull out your chair; third, smile at your deskmate and say, 'I'm back!'" Yu took a deep breath and stepped into the classroom. He pulled out his chair, turned to his deskmate Xiao Ming, and smiled, saying, "Xiao Ming, I'm back. Which notebook would you like now?" Xiao Ming smiled and pointed to the blackboard: "Yu, you're back! Quickly get your vocabulary notebook, we're about to start writing!" Yu quickly took out his notebook and smoothly caught up with the rest of the class!

🤔 Class discussion guidance questions:When returning to a regular class from a special education class, if you stand at the door in fear and space out, will you be able to keep up with the rest of the class? What three things should you do upon entering the classroom to quickly integrate into a larger class?
🎭 Four character situation mini theater 🦁Yu 🐻Jun 🐼He 🦊Jia full-staff drill
🎬 Today's drill scenario:After the special education class, the four little heroes returned to the regular class and practiced sitting down calmly, checking their progress, and greeting their peers!
🦁 Yu Calm and self-disciplined Yu
🎬 Action:Enter the regular classroom, look up at the blackboard to confirm the Chinese Language A textbook, quietly return to your seat, take out your textbook and turn to the designated page.
"Xiao Ming, I'm back!"I've already taken out Book A and turned to page 10, and I'm ready to write together!”
💡 Tips:Guide Yu to establish a highly independent ability to switch tasks back to work.
🐻 Jun A courageous and responsible young man
🎬 Action:When you return to the regular classroom, restrain your impulse to make loud noises, neatly put away your stationery, and sit up straight.
"Huh ~ back to the big class, I will sit down according to the class rules and be a good model student who listens carefully to the class! ”
💡 Tips:Guide students to regard the large class environment as a good stage for demonstrating maturity and self-discipline.
🐼 He Gentle and considerate little He
🎬 Action:Smile and greet your deskmate, take out your pencil case, and read aloud with the whole class.
"Good morning, everyone!"I read the text aloud with everyone, the voice was clear and loud!”
💡 Tips:Help He actively integrate into large group learning activities to enhance the sense of belonging to the class.
🦊 Jia Enthusiastic and rule-abiding Jia
🎬 Action:Actively help the group leader carry out classroom exercise sheets, demonstrating a proactive and enthusiastic attitude towards class service.
"Group leader, I'm here to help distribute exercise sheets!" Everyone has one piece each, our group is ready! ”
💡 Tips:Guide Jiayi's class service role to quickly integrate into the ordinary class organizational structure.

🔹 Students with Emotional Disorders (EBD)

👦 My Learning Support Classroom: A Place to Recharge My Strengths

🎯 Summary of core objectives:When faced with curious questions from their classmates in regular classes, such as, "Are you stupid for going to the gifted class?", special education students often feel ashamed, lower their heads and cry, or become angry and hit others. Instead, teach them, "That's my superpower charging station! I practice emotional braking and reading magic there!" This fosters a confident and positive response.

📖 Classroom situation adventure story island and questions Arouse empathy · Aware of challenges
🔋 Superman cape and shiny badges in the secret base!

While eating lunch, a classmate from a regular class sitting in the back row looked at He curiously and asked, "He, why are you never in the classroom on Tuesdays and Thursdays? Why do you go to that study room at the very bottom of the second-floor corridor? Is that a place for idiots?" These words struck He like a blow to the heart. Her eyes instantly reddened, and she so sadly lowered her head almost to her lunchbox, her spoon trembling in her hand. She wanted to run away on the spot. Just then, Jun, sitting next to her, suddenly stood up, puffed out her chest, and loudly proclaimed, "No way! That's the school's strongest 'Superhuman Recharging Base'! We learn there how to brake our emotions, how to be communication masters, and the teachers even teach us super memory magic!" Looking at the brave Jun, He took a deep breath, wiped away her tears, and slowly raised her head, smiling into the classmate's eyes, saying, "Yes! I practice fixing my brain that used to 'dance like Chinese characters' there. Now I recognize twice as many characters as before!" "If you have any emotional magic tricks you don't know, I can teach you!" The classmate's eyes widened in admiration: "Wow! That sounds so cool! I really want to try it out too!" The heavy weight in He's heart disappeared, replaced by a sense of pride!

🤔 Class discussion guidance questions:When others ask you why you go to the special education learning room, will crying out of inferiority or throwing a tantrum to eliminate prejudice? Confidently talk about the superpowers you learned in the learning room, and why that's the best way to win others' admiration?
🎭 Four character situation mini theater 🦁Yu 🐻Jun 🐼He 🦊Jia full-staff drill
🎬 Today's drill scenario:When faced with curious inquiries from peers about the purpose of the special education class, the four little heroes practice activating the charging station, making a proud declaration, and responding confidently and positively!
🦁 Yu Calm and self-disciplined Yu
🎬 Action:When faced with a classmate's question, look at them calmly and introduce your learning content in a clear and steady voice.
"I practice eye radar and social theater in the study classroom. That is a good place for me to upgrade my brain! ”
💡 Tips:Guide Yu to view his own special education support needs with objective facts and a confident attitude.
🐻 Jun A courageous and responsible young man
🎬 Action:Stand tall, pat your chest confidently, and enthusiastically promote the emotional braking skills learned in the special education class.
"That's the Superman base!" Now I can count to ten when I'm angry, that's the special power I developed there! ”
💡 Tips:Guide students to regard special education learning achievements as glory and break negative stereotype labels.
🐼 He Gentle and considerate little He
🎬 Action:Raise your head, look directly into your peers' eyes, smile confidently, and sincerely share your progress in reading and writing.
"I learned how to cut the dancing Chinese characters into chocolate there. I am making a lot of progress every day now!"”
💡 Tips:Help He overcome inferiority complex and build strong self-acceptance and inner self-confidence.
🦊 Jia Enthusiastic and rule-abiding Jia
🎬 Action:Show the whole class the gold superpower medal you received in the special education class, radiating positive influence.
"We learn to help and cooperate with each other in the learning classroom. Everyone is a shining hero! ”
💡 Tips:Guiding Jia demonstrates diverse values ​​with pride and wins the admiration of all peers.

🏠 Taking Turns with Siblings: Sharing Screens Fairly

🎯 Summary of core objectives:Special education students often get so fixated on the cartoons or games they want to watch that they fight fiercely with their younger siblings over remote controls or tablets, sometimes even scratching or biting each other, causing family conflicts. Guiding students to use physical timers and turn-taking agreements can help them learn to share generously.

📖 Classroom situation adventure story island and questions Arouse empathy · Aware of challenges
📺 Black remote control tug-of-war and colorful timer hourglass!

When Jun got home from school, he threw down his backpack and rushed to the living room sofa, grabbing the remote to change the channel to watch his favorite Beetle cartoon. Just then, his sister, two years younger than him, ran over, grabbed the other end of the remote, and yelled, "It's my turn to watch Peppa Pig this time! Let go!" The two of them pulled on the sofa like in a tug-of-war, tearing the remote's battery cover off. Jun, furious, raised his hand to strike his sister's arm: "I'm the older brother! Get away from me!" His mother, hearing this from the kitchen, shouted, "Jun! Stop!" Suddenly, the "friendship piggy bank" trick his teacher had taught him popped into his head—hitting his sister would cost him ten gold coins! Jun took a deep breath, withdrew his fist, and took out the "30-minute liquid color hourglass" from his special education class, placing it in the center of the TV cabinet: "Sister, let's not fight!" "Put the hourglass in the middle. You watch Peppa Pig for twenty minutes first. When the hourglass runs out, I'll watch The Beetle. No cheating allowed!" Seeing her brother being reasonable, the younger sister wiped away her tears and nodded: "Okay! Brother, you turn on the TV for me first!" A family battle turned into a harmonious sibling time amidst the ticking of the hourglass!

🤔 Class discussion guidance questions:How sad would it make your parents if you fought with your younger siblings over the TV or tablet at home? Why can taking turns using a timer make you a more likable older brother or sister?
🎭 Four character situation mini theater 🦁Yu 🐻Jun 🐼He 🦊Jia full-staff drill
🎬 Today's drill scenario:At home, the four little heroes practice starting the timer hourglass and negotiating to take turns not fighting over the TV remote control with their siblings!
🦁 Yu Calm and self-disciplined Yu
🎬 Action:Take out the tablet timer on the living room sofa, set a countdown, and quietly wait for your younger brother to finish watching an episode of the cartoon.
"The time is set!" My brother will watch for fifteen minutes first. When the time is up, he will beep and then let me play!”
💡 Tips:Guide Yu to apply strict time rules to family sibling relationship mediation.
🐻 Jun A courageous and responsible young man
🎬 Action:Pull back your fist that you want to punch, place the remote control flat in the middle of the table, and generously let your sister watch the first episode.
"Hoo~ I'm a man!" Sister, if you are young, you choose first. When the hourglass is finished, remember to watch it for me!”
💡 Tips:Guide parents to transform their impulses into caring for their younger brothers and sisters, and improve their self-esteem and self-discipline.
🐼 He Gentle and considerate little He
🎬 Action:Actively pour a glass of juice for your younger sister, sit next to her and watch Peppa Pig cartoons together, and enjoy the companionship of your sibling.
"It's fun to watch TV together!"Sister, it’s so funny to see Peppa Pig jumping in the mud pit!”
💡 Tips:Help He experience the brotherly warmth of companionship and communion, and resolve the sense of competition and opposition.
🦊 Jia Enthusiastic and rule-abiding Jia
🎬 Action:Post a family-shared schedule on the refrigerator, clearly indicating each person's designated entertainment time.
"We put the name and time on the refrigerator, one time per person, everyone is fair!"”
💡 Tips:Guide Jia to extend structured life routines into daily family management.

🥣 Helper for serving tea and dishes
🏷️ Inspiration Library Topic 6: Putian Fusion and Family Life 📌 Field:🏠 Fusion family
